picks.headline: No. 13 Texas Tech vs. No. 22 Arizona Football Game Preview and Prediction
picks.blurb: No. 13 Texas Tech vs. No. 22 Arizona Football Game Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Texas Tech Athletics Texas Tech hosts Arizona in this big time Big 12 showdown. The Texas Tech Red Raiders need to focus on boosting their offense for this one. Quarterback Will Hammond has 1,561 passing yards, but he has thrown only six touchdowns and has six interceptions on the season. Explosive running back J'Koby Williams has 619 rushing yards and 5 TDs, but if you take away the Arizona State and Oregon State games, he has been inconsistent for the Red Raiders this season. Kenny Johnson , a receiver, is the main downfield target but only has one touchdown reception this season and, besides the Houston and Arizona State games, has not had a significant impact on the Texas Tech passing attack. All three as well as some other key offensive players need to step up and have big games against Arizona to win this game. The defense has to get back to focusing and dominating like they have for a lot of the season. The Red Raiders have one of the most ball-hawking secondary units in the country, sitting near the top of NCAA FBS with 13 interceptions. Defensive lineman A.J. Holmes Jr. anchors the front seven and has 6 sacks this season. However, the Red Raiders are coming off their first loss of the season, a 37-24 loss to Cincinnati where they gave up 427 yards and gave up four passing touchdowns. They will be seeking to bounce back at home to stay undefeated at home this season. Arizona, on the other hand, has a five-game winning streak and defeated Cincinnati by a final score of 34-7. Their only loss of the season was to BYU on the road. Veteran quarterback Noah Fifita leads the Arizona Wildcats, who again have a high-efficiency passing offense, with Fifiti already having 2,064 passing yards and 18 TDs through seven games. Kedrick Reescano leads the ground game with just over 300 rushing yards and five touchdowns, while wideout Isaiah Mizell is an explosive playmaker with 493 yards and 5 TDs this season, most of which have come in the Wildcats' last two games against Iowa State and West Virginia. Linebacker Taye Brown has a team-leading 27 tackles and leads the Wildcats defense. Edge rusher Chase Kennedy leads the team in pressure rate with 4 sacks, and the Texas Tech offensive line has a tough task trying to stop him from getting to the quarterback. Arizona has a scoring defense that gives up only 16.7 points per game, but they did give up 31 points against West Virginia. Arizona recently crushed Iowa State 39-3 and has put up a total of just over 200 points in their last five games. The Wildcats are also 2-1 on the road this season heading into Lubbock for this top 25 game. The key matchup for this game will be Noah Fifita vs. the Texas Tech secondary. Fifita’s efficient throwing (almost 74% completion rate) will face immediate tests from a Red Raider defense that excels at creating takeaways via interceptions. Another major matchup in this game pits the Red Raiders offensive line against Arizona’s front seven on defense. Texas Tech’s running offense behind J’Koby Williams and Quinten Joyner will face a challenge against an Arizona front seven that is holding opponents under 110 rushing yards per game. This game also has Big 12 Championship ramifications since both teams are deadlocked at 3-1 in conference play behind undefeated Utah, and the winner is squarely in the race for a Big 12 Championship Game berth. An early game prediction for this game that may change slightly as the injury reports for both teams come out later this week, but the Red Raiders bounce back and win a very close game by a final score of Texas Tech 28, Arizona 27. Dybantsa delivers in debut Arizona vs Texas Tech Prediction: Big 12 Elimination Game? Pete Fiutak Tue, October 27, 2026 at 11:28 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Texas Tech was cruising right along, looking like the star of the Big 12 again after a 53-25 blowout over Arizona State, and then it walked into a wall at Cincinnati, losing with a 37-24 thud. Arizona has been fantastic ever since its 28-17 loss at BYU early in the season, including a 34-7 win over Cincinnati. But it still has a few nasty games to go in November. Both teams are 6-1. The winner will be set up nicely for a College Football Playoff spot if it doesn't win the Big 12 title. The loser will still be alive for the CFP if it wins out, but getting to the Big 12 Championship in a loaded conference season will be tough. Arizona vs Texas Tech: Quick Hits Texas Tech still has to go to Oklahoma State, but it doesn't have to face BYU or Utah, and the other three games against West Virginia, at Baylor, and TCU aren't bad. Arizona gets three of its final four games at home, getting TCU and Utah next before going to Kansas State and finishing up against Arizona State. Texas Tech won the most recent matchup 28-22 in 2024 and is 5-2-1 in the series going back to 1975. How To Watch Arizona vs Texas Tech Arizona at Texas Tech Date: Saturday, October 31, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Galaxy Stadium, Lubbock, TX – Week 9 Schedule, Game Previews – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predicting the First CFP Top 25 – CFN Week 9 Expert Picks Why Arizona Will Win For the second time all year, Texas Tech played someone who could run well, and Cincinnati went off in the 13-point win. Houston can run. It ran 37 times for 175 yards against the Red Raiders, and lost when it couldn't hit a late two-point conversion. Cincinnati wasn't exactly more physical, but it found space on the way to a 255-yard day with big run after big run. Arizona's running game isn't a killer, but it's more than effective enough, working hand-in-hand with super-accurate quarterback Noah Fifita and an offense that's great at keeping the chains moving. Why Texas Tech Will Win Arizona doesn't take the ball away enough, and that matters in a huge way here. The Wildcats forced two takeaways in the win over Washington State, and two more in the win over West Virginia. That's about it, coming up with six on the year. Texas Tech has a huge problem with turnovers, with three against Cincinnati, two against Houston, and ten in the last five games. Don't turn it over, or at least stay even in the mistake battle, and the Red Raiders should be fine. Texas Tech has a great balance to its attack, and it needs to mix it up. BYU and West Virginia – in very different ways – both showed it's possible to move the ball efficiently against the Wildcat defense. Arizona vs Texas Tech Prediction, Betting Lines Is Arizona ready to show that it's really and truly a player, or will Texas Tech wipe away the Cincinnati loss like it was just a blip? It'll be a little of both, as Arizona controls the clock and tempo for the first half, but Texas Tech gets the pass rush working early in the second half. It'll be rough for the Red Raiders without pressuring Fifita, and they won't do enough of it over the final ten minutes. Texas Tech expert previews the Arizona football game, makes a score prediction
picks.blurb: Texas Tech expert previews the Arizona Wildcats football game, makes a score prediction | Arizona Desert Swarm Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo An Arizona Wildcats Community Arizona Desert Swarm October 29, 2026 Arizona Desert Swarm Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Arizona Basketball Arizona Football Arizona Softball Arizona Recruiting Arizona Soccer Arizona Volleyball Arizona Baseball Arizona Gymnastics Arizona in the Pros Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Arizona Football Odds Arizona Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Arizona Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Arizona Football College football has one of the longest offseasons of any sport, which lends itself to certain players and teams generating a lot of hype and attention. Texas Tech falls squarely in that category, as its seemingly unlimited resources thanks to billionaire booster Cody Campbell made it a go-to place for top transfers out of the portal. But that also led to the ill-fated acquisition of quarterback Brendan Sorsby , who after leaving Cincinnati for Tech was revealed to have bet on college sports. Sorsby was banned by the NCAA, later reinstated, but the backlash led to him leaving the program before ever playing a game. Despite that, Tech was unbeaten before losing last week, dropping to No. 13 in the AP poll and into a tie for second place in the Big 12 with, among other teams, Arizona. That in effect makes Saturday’s matchup an unofficial elimination game for the conference title race. To better understand the Red Raiders, we reached out to Seth Jungman of Staking the Plains for some insight and a score prediction. Below are his eloquent answers to our inarticulate questions: AZ Desert Swarm: Outside of the irony of the first loss coming to Cincinnati, what were the biggest contributors to Texas Tech falling from the ranks of the unbeatens? Seth Jungman: “It’s the thing that I think Texas Tech fans have known, but maybe the national media wasn’t paying attention. I think most fans have known that the offense simply wasn’t very good and the defense isn’t as good as it was last year. Will Hammond is fine, but there’s a reason why the staff went out to get Brendan Sorsby before the season. They knew he probably wasn’t ready, but things happened and here we are. Also, I think it’s incredibly evident that the players who were part of this defense last year were truly special, particularly Jacob Rodriguez, David Bailey, and Romello Height. Getting to the quarterback to wreck offenses was the cheat code last year and this year, that’s simply not happening.” It’s fair to say that Will Hammond was not the first choice to lead this offense. How do you think he has performed to this point? What are his best attributes and where does he lack most? “I thought last week against Arizona State he took a step forward, but against Cincinnati he took two steps back. His best attributes is that he is a natural leader and he wants the ball in his hands and he wants to be the guy. My biggest problem with him is that I think he makes bad game management decisions. Knowing that the team needs points, he’ll heave the ball towards the end zone with a low chance of completion rather than take the play that keeps the drive alive. His lack of understanding of knowing when to take chances and when to churn yards is what bothers me the most.” What is the likelihood that Cameron Dickey will be back for this game? How would that impact the run game and the way J’Koby Williams, who has run for 680 yards and five touchdowns, get used? “I think chances are very good that he returns. It’s been about four weeks from the dreaded high-ankle sprain and that’s about the time. I don’t think it was a bad sprain so this game would seem about right and he was out doing some drills this past week. What Dickey offers is a guy that’s going to bruise and batter the opposing defense while Williams will break a 40-yard run in what looks like a lost play. Quinten Joyner has tried to fill that roll for Dickey, but it’s not the same. Joyner is coming off of ACL surgery and he doesn’t have the same burst he had at USC. I think the staff will likely get back to that Dickey-Williams rotation as soon as possible.” Texas Tech is second in FBS in passes intercepted (13) but has also given up 16 TD passes and is ranked third-worst in the Big 12 in pass defense. How do you expect the defense to try and stop Noah Fifita? “As mentioned above, the Texas Tech defense last year was getting to the quarterback so quickly that teams simply could not function offensively. This year . . . not so much. Fifita has rounded out to be such a good quarterback, I truly expect him to have a very good day. There’s almost no difference between his home and road stats, three picks on the road and just one at home, and he’s throwing for nearly 300 yards every time he steps on the field. That’s the kind of consistency that you expect from a senior and with Fifita’s ability to run to keep the defense honest, I expect him to do what he’s done all year long.” Who are the top defensive players that Arizona has to be most concerned with? “Defensive tackle AJ Holmes is an absolute unit and there aren’t a ton of defensive tackles that truly rush the passer, but he’s one of them. The linebacking corps is incredibly solid with Ben Roberts, John Curry and Austin Romaine. I’ll also add in Brice Pollock at cornerback. The pass defense is struggling a bit, but he’s a solid cornerback that can make plays.” Considering all the money that was spent on this team, and all the national attention it has brought on itself—thanks, Cody Campbell!—does it feel like the season is on the line in this game? How do you expect Tech to respond to that last performance? “As you have already recognized, this team is a quarterback short of maybe what it could have been. I try not to involve myself in the offseason drama. The whole thing was a mess and handled poorly. I think we’ve all moved on, but I know it still lingers and I think that Sorsby would have made a significant difference in the offense. For what Joey McGuire preaches, yes, the season is on the brink because the goal is to win the Big 12 and make the playoffs. I don’t know that a Big 12 team with two losses makes the playoff and I also don’t think that a 2-loss Big 12 team makes the championship. “I do expect Texas Tech to play much better than what they did against Cincinnati and I think it will be a much more competitive game. I also realize that Arizona’s defense is no joke and the Texas Tech offense has really only played well against defenses that aren’t very good. The offense and defense for the Red Raiders have a lot to prove against Arizona.” Prediction time. Does Arizona end the Red Raiders’ 12-game home win streak and continue its push toward the Big 12 title game or does Texas Tech get back on track? Give us a score pick. “My gut tells me that this will be an incredibly close game and Vegas thinks so as well. With a touchdown advantage, the line now sits at Texas Tech -3.5. I tend to agree, that despite the flaws that were on display against Cincinnati, I think Texas Tech does win the game, but I’d take Arizona and those points. Texas Tech vs. Arizona: Prediction, Pick and Preview
picks.blurb: Arizona vs. Texas Tech Prediction, Pick and Odds for Week 9 Teams Arizona Wildcats Arizona State Sun Devils Cincinnati Bearcats Colorado Buffaloes Houston Cougars Iowa State Cyclones Kansas Jayhawks Kansas State Wildcats Oklahoma State Cowboys TCU Horned Frogs Texas Tech Red Raiders West Virginia Mountaineers Former Foes Missouri Tigers Nebraska Cornhuskers Oklahoma Sooners Texas A&M Aggies Texas Longhorns Recruiting Football Transfer Portal Video Watch on YouTube Listen on Apple Listen on Spotify Forum Members Login Heartland College Sports – An Independent Big 12 Today Blog | College Football News | Big 12 Today The Arizona Wildcats and Texas Tech Red Raiders meet on Saturday in Lubbock in a Top 25 showdown that could have major implications on the Big 12 Championship race. Both teams enter Week 9 at 6-1 overall and 3-1 in Big 12 play, but they're coming off completely different Saturdays. Arizona made another statement by crushing Iowa State 39-3, while Texas Tech suffered its first loss of the season in a 37-24 road defeat at Cincinnati. Now, Texas Tech returns home to a place where it has won 12 straight games, while Arizona gets another opportunity to prove it belongs among the top contenders in the Big 12. The matchup also features an intriguing battle between Noah Fifita and an aggressive Texas Tech defense that leads the country with five pick-sixes this season. Here is everything you need to know about Arizona vs. Texas Tech in Week 9, including our prediction and pick for Saturday's Big 12 showdown. Texas Tech vs. Arizona Odds Spread: Texas Tech -3.5 Over/Under: 54.5 Moneyline: Arizona +134/Texas Tech -160 Odds as of Tuesday afternoon. Odds are subject to change. The Biggest Question: Arizona's Passing Game vs. Texas Tech's Defense? The Red Raiders' defense has been underwhelming, at best. Texas Tech ranks 14th in the Big 12 Conference in passing yards allowed per game, ranking only ahead of Cincinnati and West Virginia. Now, this secondary does have 13 takeaways, which is tops in the Big 12. But that also tells me that they may be too aggressive , at times. And now they have to slow down Noah Fifita, who doesn't make many mistakes. He's thrown 18 touchdowns to just four interceptions this season and has the deepest wide receiver corps in the entire Big 12. Whoever wins this match up will win the game. Houston vs. Utah Prediction and Pick Prediction: Arizona 31, Texas Tech 24 Texas Tech was exposed last week at Cincinnati. Yes, they have talent, but they haven't been able to put it all together this season. And after Saturday, there's no evidence that it's magically going to happen against one of the most underrated teams in the country, Arizona, who is playing some of the best football in America right now. Since losing to BYU on the road (a game they led in the second half), Arizona has won five-straight games by an average of nearly 24 points. I haven't even talked about the other side of the ball, where Arizona is Top 5 in passing defense in yards allowed per game, and ranked 3rd in the Big 12 in yards allowed per carry (3.1). The front seven has been outstanding, as that impressive run defense has done it against the Top 2 rushing offenses in the league (West Virginia, Cincinnati). They've racked up 24 sacks in seven games, good for second in the Big 12, and now take on a Texas Tech offensive line that has been spotty, at best, throughout the season. Also, in a game that could come down to the final drive or two, Arizona's red zone defense ranks tops in the Big 12, while Texas Tech comes in at No. 14. And as the game wears on, the Tech defense could get worn down. Tech is second-to-last in the Big 12 in Time of Possession, while Arizona is in the Top 5, this despite having a pass-heavy offense. The icing on the cake on my pick? Special teams. Arizona is the best punt returning team in the Big 12. Texas Tech ranks 13th. These little things in a tough Top 25 match up can be the difference. And they will be come Saturday in Lubbock. And if you want to know where the sharp money is: 62% of the tickets are on Texas Tech, but over 80% of the money is on Arizona. The line opened up at Arizona +4.5 and is down to +3.5. If you can still get more than a field goal, jump on it. Arizona wins. Arizona covers. picks.headline: Arizona football at Texas Tech score predictions
picks.blurb: Arizona Wildcats football at Texas Tech Red Raiders score predictions | Arizona Desert Swarm Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo An Arizona Wildcats Community Arizona Desert Swarm October 29, 2026 Arizona Desert Swarm Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Arizona Basketball Arizona Football Arizona Softball Arizona Recruiting Arizona Soccer Arizona Volleyball Arizona Baseball Arizona Gymnastics Arizona in the Pros Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Arizona Football Odds Arizona Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Arizona Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Arizona Football Arizona has been one of the hottest teams in the country the past six weeks, winning five straight (all by double digits) to climb into the national rankings and near the top of the Big 12 standings. But now comes the Wildcats’ toughest test since Week 2, a trip to Lubbock to take on No. 13 Texas Tech. The Red Raiders (6-1, 3-1 Big 12) are coming off a 37-24 loss at Cincinnati, whom the UA beat 34-7 at home on Oct. 3. How will the Wildcats do in this West Texas showdown? Our staff makes its predictions. Kim Doss — Texas Tech wins 28-27 Arizona has one of the top offenses in the country, landing in the top 50 in a number of categories: 2 nd in completion percentage (.738), 3 rd in third down conversion percentage (.547), 28 th in first downs, 42 nd in red zone offense (.889), 21 st in scoring offense (36.1), 12 th in team passing efficiency (169.66), and 17 th in total offense (459.4). When looking through the offensive stats, a comp for this game starts to come into focus. Houston keeps popping up in a similar position for most categories. The stats are not identical, and each team has a few strengths that the other lacks, but overall, they are fairly comparable offenses. That is relevant this week because the Cougars are the only ranked team that this week’s opponent has faced. Texas Tech took on No. 18 Houston the third week of the season. Like Saturday’s contest, it was played in Lubbock. The Red Raiders squeaked out a 28-26 win. They won their next three games handily against lesser competition before the surprising blowout upset by Cincinnati last week. It all suggests that TTU can be pushed, and perhaps even be beaten, in its home stadium. Arizona has the offense to compete. It showed last week that it can utterly shut down a team that averages just under 26 points per game. The Wildcats won’t hold TTU to three points, but they are good enough to keep this one up for grabs until the end. Ezra Amacher — Arizona wins 27- 24 Arizona is walking into a hornet’s nest in Lubbock after Texas Tech got embarrassed Cincinnati. One of the major storylines in college football this week is whether Texas Tech billionaire booster Cody Campbell is going force any personnel issues if the Red Raiders’ struggles persist. Everyone in a 100-mile radius of Lubbock knows that there is a lot more on the line Saturday than your typical Big 12 game. Another Texas Tech loss would knock the Red Raiders out of playoff contention. All that setup is to say that Arizona is facing a team that will be playing with its pants on fire. Even so, I think Noah Fifita does enough for the Wildcats to pull off one of the program’s biggest wins of the last decade. Texas Tech on paper has one of the top defenses in the Big 12, but the unit hasn’t totally lived up to the billing. Texas Tech gives up 266 passing yards per game, which is third-worst in the conference. Arizona’s passing offense is one of the best in the country, and with the Wildcats getting more receivers reps each game, I feel confident that they can successfully throw the ball Saturday. Arizona’s biggest obstacle to winning will be converting scoring opportunities on offense and limited the Red Raiders offense when they get down the field. Texas Tech’s opponents have scored on 83% of red zone drives, which is also third-worst in the Big 12. By contrast, Arizona’s red zone defense is first in the Big 12, allowing points on 67% of drives. I expect the red zone advantage to favor Arizona, allowing the Wildcats to leave Lubbock with a close win. Adam Green — Texas Tech wins 34 -24 I’d feel better had Tech not lost to Cincinnati last week. On paper Texas Tech has a better (or at least more expensive) roster. This game is in Lubbock, and it is also on Halloween. Aside from what happens on the field, there is plenty surrounding this matchup that just gives the vibe of there potentially being too much to overcome for Arizona. That said, the small spread and general vibe around each program lends itself to the idea that Arizona could leave that game Saturday with a victory and a clear path to the Big 12 title game. If Arizona can win the turnover battle and limit big plays from Tech there is then reason to believe that Noah Fifita and the Wildcats offense can move the ball. Not settling for field goal attempts will be important, of course. So yeah, Arizona could win this game. The Cats are playing excellent football and are no doubt confident they can win a big matchup on the road. But in my mind the home team will come out focused and fired up following its first loss and the environment will be such that the visitors cannot afford a slow start or to make mistakes. Asking any team to play a perfect game to have a chance to win is both unfair and unrealistic, which is why I just can’t predict an upset in this one. Juan Serrano — Texas Tech wins 31-27 It isn’t unrealistic to think that Arizona can win in Lubbock, this is a team playing with a high level of confidence and execution of its game plan. Led by Noah Fifita , the offense is moving the ball with ease and scoring almost whenever it wants to. While it is still lacking explosiveness, the run game is coming on slowly. However, this is a Red Raiders defense that is very opportunistic and athletic. It forces its opponents into mistakes that aren’t usually made. If Arizona can keep it clean on offense it will have a chance to win the game. The defense plays a lot better inside Casino Del Sol Stadium and it showed last week. Now on the road at Lubbock, it will face a challenge similar to what it saw in Provo. If the Wildcats are going to be in a position to win they will need force turnovers. Arizona only had two interceptions and five fumbles on the season, that number will need to rise on Saturday. If this game was being played in Tucson I’d probably be rolling with the Wildcats. It’s not a long road trip to Lubbock but it will end up feeling like a long trip. Texas Tech will rebound from the loss to Cincinnati with a win over Arizona. Brandon Combs — Arizona wins 31-21 I’m going to go against my pre-season prediction and my better judgement here. This is 100% a game Arizona can win, and I think they do on Saturday. Texas Tech’s defense is legit. Ben Roberts and Austin Romaine are phenomenal linebackers, combining for 102 tackles, 10 TFL, 2 sacks and 3 interceptions on the year. John Curry and Brice Pollock are fantastic cover corners. AJ Holmes is a monster on the interior defensive line and leads the conference with 5.5 sacks on the year. So why would I pick Arizona? It’s because the Red Raider offense leaves a lot to be desired. Quarterback Will Hammond has not been great this season. He is completing 68% of his passes and only has 6 touchdown passes to go along with 6 picks. Hammond can make plays with his legs but I don’t foresee Arizona’s defense having an issue there. They do have some good running backs with J’koby Williams , Quinten Joyner and Cameron Dickey . Williams is sitting at a measly 7.2 yards per carry on the season and has 619 yards on the ground and 5 touchdowns to his name. Coy Eakin and Kenny Johnson are Tech’s top two receivers, with Johnson sitting just under 500 yards and a touchdown. With all that, I believe the Arizona defense can stymy the Red Raider offense. The key will be how Noah Fifita and Seth Doege plan and execute around Tech’s solid defense. Last week showed that this defense can be taken advantage of and can be scored on. If Noah plays a clean game, I don’t see how Tech can win against the Wildcat defense. Brian Pedersen — Texas Tech wins 24-20 Arizona has a 5-game win streak in consecutive seasons for the first time since 1992-93, but the difference between this year’s run and the one in 2025 is when it has happened. Last fall the Wildcats shook off back-to-back heartbreaking losses to BYU and Houston to catch fire and win out the rest of the regular season, while this time around the solid play has been happening pretty much from the outset. But Texas Tech is far better than any of the teams the UA faced during the win streak, even the Cincinnati team that beat the Red Raiders. Tech has won 12 in a row in Lubbock, where offensive coordinator Seth Doege will be returning to his old stomping grounds. And the opponent has a very high-priced roster, one that to this point hasn’t lived up to expectations. This is a game that Arizona can’t afford to fall behind by two scores in, which means keeping mistakes to a minimum. Assuming Noah Fifita has his patented solid performance, this will come down to who capitalizes on their chances the most. away.headline: Arizona football: CB Jay’Vion Cole to miss Texas Tech game, 2 injured receivers could return
away.blurb: CB Jay’Vion Cole is listed as out on the first availability report issued by the Big 12 Conference, one of four players ruled out for the matchup with the 13th-ranked Red Raiders.. Also out are tight end Shane King and defensive linemen Kevin Moore and Ezra Funa , the latter having not played yet this season. On the offensive side, receivers Chris Hunter and Giovanni Richardson are listed as questionable. Both have missed the past two games after getting hurt Oct. 3 vs. Cincinnati, the same game fellow WR Tre Spivey suffered a season-ending injury. Tight end Cole Rusk , who has been out several games, is listed as doubtful. Also listed as questionable are running back Ismail Mahdi and linebacker Max Harris but not because of injury. Both are seeking another emergency injunction to restore their eligibility after each appeared in a few games earlier this season. For Texas Tech, running back Cameron Dickey is listed as questionable. He’s missed the last two games with an ankle injury. Arizona could get back a pair of injured wide receivers for Saturday’s Top 25 showdown at Texas Tech, but it will also be without its lockdown corner Cole had started the first seven games this season, allowing only 16 catches on 30 targets, and is among the top-graded corners in the Big 12. In his absence the UA is likely to start Dwight Bootle II, who has been part of a 3-man rotation at the two corner spots with Cole and Tyrese Boss. Slot DB Malcolm Hartzog Jr. could also see time at corner.

Coming off a road loss to Minnesota in which they turned the ball over four times, the Hawkeyes look to bounce back against the Badgers, and my Wisconsin vs. Iowa prediction targets Iowa (-3.5) to cover in a low-scoring Week 9 matchup. Here are my latest college football picks ahead of this 12 p.m. ET kickoff (FOX) on Saturday, Oct. 31. TOP PICK Who will win Wisconsin vs Iowa: Iowa -3.5 It's hard to lay the -3.5 in a game where the total is sitting at 37.5. However, this is a home game for the Iowa Hawkeyes , and we all know Kinnick Stadium is one of the toughest places to come out alive, let alone with a win. Iowa is coming off two straight road games, the latest being a 13-10 loss to Minnesota as a 7.5-point favorite. The Hawkeyes outgained Minnesota by nearly 80 yards, but turnovers proved to be their downfall. Iowa turned the ball over four times and still lost by just three points. This week, the Hawkeyes should clean up those mistakes and be ready to take on a Wisconsin Badgers team coming off a big win over No. 16 USC. I wouldn't play this any higher than the current number. I'd love -2.5, but -3 is definitely playable if you can get it. Wisconsin vs Iowa Over/Under pick: Under 37.5 Neither team is allowing more than 16 points per game this season , and both rank top 20 in yards allowed per game. Despite Iowa getting off to a slightly faster start than Wisconsin, points should be at a premium in this matchup. Iowa's defense should be able to force plenty of three-and-outs, ranking 20th in third-down defense while allowing opponents to convert just 32.95% of the time. Wisconsin leans more heavily on its run game, which will face an Iowa defense allowing just 2.5 yards per carry. On the other side, Iowa has leaned more on its passing attack, which will face a Wisconsin defense ranked 30th in passing yards allowed per game. By Cory Nightingale Published: Oct 29, 2026 · 1:16 PM EDT Greg McElroy broke down what he thinks will happen when old SEC rivals Auburn and Ole Miss get together in a Week 9 matchup on Saturday that will pit 2 teams desperate to get back on the winning track. During McElroy's game-by-game breakdown on his Always College Football podcast earlier this week, the former Alabama quarterback turned analyst talked about his impressions of No. 12 Ole Miss (5-2, 3-2 SEC), which is coming off a heartbreaking loss last week at Texas , and unranked Auburn (4-3, 2-3 SEC), which was steamrolled at home in Week 8 by LSU. The Tigers have been on an SEC roller-coaster ride the past few weeks, winning at Georgia in Week 7 before coming home and laying an egg against LSU in that Week 8 dud. Meanwhile, there are the Rebels, who nearly erased a 3-touchdown deficit in Austin last Saturday night before falling short to Arch Manning and the Longhorns. away.blurb: WEDNESDAY Ole Miss vs. Auburn Injury Report: Crawford, Davis Questionable; Lacy Out ‘I've got to go out there and earn it’: Hunter Elliott returns with something to prove as Ole Miss opens fall OXFORD, Miss. – The first SEC availability report of Auburn week is out, and No. 12 Ole Miss has two key starters listed as questionable for Saturday. Cornerback Jalyn Crawford and left tackle Terez Davis are both questionable on the initial report, released at 7:10 p.m. CT on Wednesday. Running back Kewan Lacy is out, as expected, after dislocating his shoulder in last week's loss at Texas. Jalyn Crawford questionable after big night at Texas Pete Golding said Monday that Crawford “played his best game” at Texas and is “starting to show who we thought he was.” Losing him would be a big blow to a secondary that is already thin. Safety Edwin Joseph is out again as he works his way back from a procedure, and Golding said Monday he did not “feel great” about Joseph's chances this week. Safety MJ Preston, cornerback Cedrick Beavers, cornerback Iverson McCoy and safety Nascar McCoy are also out. Terez Davis questionable, but trending up Davis missed the Texas game after being a game-time decision, and he is questionable again to start the week. But Golding sounded confident Monday that his left tackle will be back. “Probably could have done it, but we didn't know what it was going to look like after and could have made it worse,” Golding said of holding Davis out in Austin. “So that's one definitely that we feel like, throughout this week, that we'll get back for this weekend.” Without Davis, Connor Howes moved to left tackle and Tommy Kinsler started at right tackle, and the line did not allow a sack. Howes and center Brycen Sanders are both listed as probable. Kewan Lacy out, Makhi Frazier steps in Ole Miss will also be without wide receivers Izaiah Hartrup and Kervin Johnson Jr., linebacker Ant Davis Jr. and offensive lineman Emanuel Faulkner. Defensive tackle Michai Boireau is probable. Auburn's list is short. Offensive lineman Tai Buster and tight end Hunter Herring are out, and wide receiver Jeremiah Koger is questionable. The SEC releases availability reports on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday evenings of game week, with a final update on game day. The Thursday report comes out at 7:10 p.m. CT, and the final report is due about 90 minutes before Saturday's 11:45 a.m. kickoff. away.headline: Auburn head coach Alex Golesh gives key injury update on Tai Buster
away.blurb: Sophomore Tai Buster was expected to be a key piece of Auburn's offensive line rotation this season, but a preseason setback has kept him away from the field . This week, Auburn head coach Alex Golesh gave a positive report for Buster's availability, saying he could be available to play as early as a few weeks. “Tai (Buster) has worked his tail off. I give Tai a lot of credit. He is working through return to play," Golesh said Monday. "The hope is that here in a couple of weeks, we get him fully integrated in practice, and it gives us a chance to see where he is." For injured players, it can take days or weeks to catch up and return to their routine, but Golesh says that will not be the case for Buster. Buster has remained immersed in practice and should return to full speed quickly. "He’s been engaged; I give him a lot of credit again, he’s been engaged," Golesh said. "He’s itching to get back out there. I thought when he got banged up, he was competing at a high level. We’re excited to get him back here soon.” Adding Buster to the rotation will not solve every issue the offensive line faces, but having an extra body will help keep linemen, especially at guard, fresh during Auburn's final stretch of regular-season games. The Tigers will be without Buster for their next game, Saturday at Ole Miss, but he could return in November to assist Auburn with their pursuit of bowl eligibility. home.headline: Another SEC game, another crowded Ole Miss injury report
home.blurb: One of the biggest storylines to watch before kickoff Saturday won't involve Auburn at all. It'll be who Ole Miss has available. The Rebels could be without several key contributors when they host Auburn, with offensive tackle Terez Davis and cornerback Jalyn Crawford listed as questionable. Safety Edwin Joseph and running back Kewan Lacy have already been ruled out. Those are two big losses, but not unexpected ones . Davis is the biggest name to monitor. The veteran offensive tackle missed last week's loss to Texas, and his status remains uncertain heading into the weekend. If he's unable to play, Ole Miss will once again have to adjust along an offensive line that has spent much of the season searching for consistency and continuity. That could become even more complicated if Brycen Sanders or Connor Howes see their statuses downgraded from probable. The secondary also enters the game with some uncertainty. Crawford's availability is still in question, while Joseph continues working his way back from ankle surgery. The veteran safety has been rehabbing daily, but his recovery has taken longer than the Rebels initially hoped, keeping one of their most experienced defensive backs off the field. Lacy will also miss Saturday's matchup as he continues recovering from a shoulder injury. His absence will put a larger workload on the rest of Ole Miss' running back room as the Rebels look to establish more balance offensively against an Auburn team that has been one of the SEC's most unpredictable groups this season. home.headline: WEDNESDAY Ole Miss vs. Auburn Injury Report: Crawford, Davis Questionable; Lacy Out
home.blurb: WEDNESDAY Ole Miss vs. Auburn Injury Report: Crawford, Davis Questionable; Lacy Out ‘I've got to go out there and earn it’: Hunter Elliott returns with something to prove as Ole Miss opens fall OXFORD, Miss. – The first SEC availability report of Auburn week is out, and No. 12 Ole Miss has two key starters listed as questionable for Saturday. Cornerback Jalyn Crawford and left tackle Terez Davis are both questionable on the initial report, released at 7:10 p.m. CT on Wednesday. Running back Kewan Lacy is out, as expected, after dislocating his shoulder in last week's loss at Texas. Jalyn Crawford questionable after big night at Texas Pete Golding said Monday that Crawford “played his best game” at Texas and is “starting to show who we thought he was.” Losing him would be a big blow to a secondary that is already thin. Safety Edwin Joseph is out again as he works his way back from a procedure, and Golding said Monday he did not “feel great” about Joseph's chances this week. Safety MJ Preston, cornerback Cedrick Beavers, cornerback Iverson McCoy and safety Nascar McCoy are also out. Terez Davis questionable, but trending up Davis missed the Texas game after being a game-time decision, and he is questionable again to start the week. But Golding sounded confident Monday that his left tackle will be back. “Probably could have done it, but we didn't know what it was going to look like after and could have made it worse,” Golding said of holding Davis out in Austin. “So that's one definitely that we feel like, throughout this week, that we'll get back for this weekend.” Without Davis, Connor Howes moved to left tackle and Tommy Kinsler started at right tackle, and the line did not allow a sack. Howes and center Brycen Sanders are both listed as probable. Kewan Lacy out, Makhi Frazier steps in Ole Miss will also be without wide receivers Izaiah Hartrup and Kervin Johnson Jr., linebacker Ant Davis Jr. and offensive lineman Emanuel Faulkner. Defensive tackle Michai Boireau is probable. Auburn's list is short. Offensive lineman Tai Buster and tight end Hunter Herring are out, and wide receiver Jeremiah Koger is questionable. The SEC releases availability reports on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday evenings of game week, with a final update on game day. The Thursday report comes out at 7:10 p.m. CT, and the final report is due about 90 minutes before Saturday's 11:45 a.m. kickoff. picks.headline: Odds Have Changed for Georgia Football vs. Florida Gators
picks.blurb: Odds Have Changed for Georgia Football vs. Florida Gators Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS ATHENS - Odds have been updated to Georgia Football’s massive clash with the Florida Gators 48 hours before the rivals face off in Atlanta. The Bulldogs and Gators are playing a one-off game in Atlanta this season , and one next year in Tampa as Jacksonville (the traditional home for this game) rebuilds its stadium. The anticipation for the game is growing as the weekend grows near. What’s also growing is the betting line for the game. On Sunday FanDuel listed the Bulldogs as a 9.5-point favorite over the Gators. DraftKings had UGA as a 10.5-point favorite in the contest. Both betting houses now have Georgia as a 12.5-point favorite to win the game. The move in the line is a fairly significant one - placing the game firmly into double-digit territory. Of course, betting lines are only an indication of what experts feel is expected to happen - they are not a guarantee of an outcome. There are two reasons the line has be crept up over the week. First, both of Florida’s quarterbacks are injured in some form. Athens-area native Aaron Philo started the first six games of the Gators’ season, but missed Florida’s 27-24 win at Texas with a shoulder injury. Tramell Jones started for the Gators in that game and guided the Gators to an upset in Austin. Jones has “wear-and-tear” injuries. Georgia football TE Jaden Reddell celebrates with Georgia football RB Chauncey Bowens after scoring a touchdown against Vanderbilt. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Florida coach Jon Sumrall said Monday that he would not name a starter at that time. Florida coach Jon Sumrall said Monday that he would not name a starter at that time. “Both guys are available - believe in both guys,” Sumrall told reporters. “Not going to name a starter today. We need both those guys to be ready to play.” Both Gator quarterbacks were listed as questionable Wednesday night on the SEC’s mandated injury report. In addition, Georgia got very good news with an upgrade for running back Chauncey Bowens, who was upgraded to questionable from out, which is where he’s been the last few weeks. Bowens scored the game-winning touchdown against the Gators last year in Jacksonville. Second, there was likely some overreaction to Georgia’s upset loss to Auburn at home, and the Gators’ upset win on the road at Florida. Most of the summer this game was listed around the 12-point mark. Florida’s play early in the season dropped the number under ten points, but that recovered to back over double digits after Florida was blown out in back-to-back losses to Missouri and South Carolina. But only twice in modern history has a double-digit favorite lost this game (1997 and 2014). In both upsets turnovers and a robust run game powered the underdog to an unexpected win. Since 2010, the Bulldogs have been favored to beat the Gators 13 times in the last 16 games. Georgia is 11-5 straight up against the Gators since then - losing in overtime as a one-point favorite in 2010, a 10-point favorite in 2014, a 3-point underdog in 2015, a 6.5-point underdog in 2016 and a 3-point favorite in 2020. On average the Dawgs have been a 6.5-point favorite to beat Florida since 2010. The team that runs the ball better in the World’s Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party is 15-1 since 2010 (2020 - Florida, 44-28). Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. For the first time in the history of the World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party, Florida and Georgia will play in Atlanta at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, with kickoff slated for Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET (ABC). The Bulldogs are 11.5-point favorites, and my Florida vs. Georgia prediction and college football picks expect Kirby Smart's team to take advantage of Jon Sumrall's defense in his first Cocktail Party. Who will win Florida vs Georgia: Georgia -11.5 Kirby Smart has owned the Florida vs. Georgia rivalry recently, winning eight of the last nine games. While he's just 5-4 against the spread in those games, his Bulldogs have the advantage against a sporadic Florida team. But without knowing which version of Florida we'll get, I would only take the Bulldogs up to -12.5 . Georgia's defense is far more trustworthy than Florida's, ranking 14th nationally in available yards percentage (35.7%) , 21st in defensive success rate (35.4%), and holding six of seven opponents to 20 or fewer points. With athletes like Chris Cole and Ellis Robinson IV, Georgia is well-equipped to deal with Buster Faulkner's misdirection-heavy offense. Plus, the Gators' top two QBs ( Aaron Philo , Tramell Jones Jr. ) are questionable , and while I expect them to play, it could impact their consistency. In a high-scoring game, Georgia's defense will make enough stops to cover. TOP PICK Florida vs Georgia Over/Under pick: Over 54.5 Georgia has been an Over machine this season, hitting it in six of seven games, despite its defense allowing just 15.9 points per game. I like the Over to hit at 55.5 or better for the fifth time in the last seven Cocktail Parties, especially given Faulkner's familiarity with Smart and Georgia's defense. Faulkner worked for Smart at Georgia for three years before spending the last three seasons as Georgia Tech's offensive coordinator; his offenses averaged 24.6 points and 392 yards against the Bulldogs. With one of the top running backs in the country in Jadan Baugh , who ranks top 10 in forced missed tackles (40), Florida should score 20+. Its defense will do the rest of the job for the Over. Florida has one of the worst defenses in the Power Four, r anking 125th in the country in defensive success rate (49.5%) , and it hasn't played an offense as efficient as Georgia's yet this season. Florida vs Georgia combo Some weeks Florida looks like a College Football Playoff team (against Ole Miss and Texas ), and other weeks it looks like it might not win eight games (against Missouri and South Carolina ). Which version will come to play in the World's Largest Cocktail Party? If Auburn hadn't improbably upset the Bulldogs the last time they played, they would probably be closer to 14.5-point favorites because of Florida's defensive struggles and offensive injuries. Coming out of a bye, I expect Smart to have Georgia ready to roll in a rivalry game he's dominated and to pull away in the second half against a Florida defense that ranks second-worst in havoc rate in the SEC (14.5%). This time the Bulldogs are listed as a 10.5-point favorite to topple the Gators in Atlanta on Halloween according to Draft Kings . It is another in a string of games where the Bulldogs have been favorites to beat their biggest SEC rival. Georgia has not been an underdog against the Gators since 2016 - the first year Kirby Smart took over as the head coach in Athens. Should the line remain unchanged at kickoff it would be the sixth time since that year that Georgia has been a double-digit favorite to win the game. Georgia's 24-20 win over Gators in Jacksonville last fall was the first time UGA had been favored by fewer than ten points in five seasons. One of the keys to success for Kirby Smart's program over his tenure in Athens has been the Dawgs' ability to slow or even stop the Gators running the ball effectively. Georgia football RB Nate Frazier (3) pushes off Florida Gators defensive back Cormani McClain. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Florida has not eclipsed the 120-yard mark on the ground since going for 161 in a 34-7 loss to the Dawg in 2021. Florida has been up and down running the ball this season - even with one of the best running backs in the nation... Jadan Baugh. Baugh has been solid against the Dawgs - going for 136 yards on 32 carries with a touchdown. With the Gators' quarterback situation in flux, Baugh might be the singularly-important player in the game. South Carolina and Missouri slowed the Atlanta native in their two wins against the Gators. But against Texas, Baugh was a workhorse again - scoring once on the ground after carrying the ball 25 times for 91 yards. Baugh blistered Auburn (162 yards; 3 TDs) and Ole Miss (142 yards; 3 TDs) earlier this season. Georgia is 7-4 all time when allowing a 100-yard rusher under Kirby Smart. Georgia had a tremendous start to the season defending the run, but has had back-to-back games on run defense that are as bad as they have had dating back to the end of the 2024 season. The Bulldogs have only covered once in the last four games against the Gators - in 2023 thanks to a late-game touchdown from Dwight Phillips. This is the first time since 2018 that UGA is coming off a loss going into a scheduled bye week. The Dawgs are 17-3 all time after losses and 12-3 after a bye under Kirby Smart. The Dawgs and Gators meet in Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta for the first time ever. The game, which is traditionally held in Jacksonville, is on a two-year hiatus from there so that massive renovations can take place to upgrade the facility there. Date, time, TV, prediction for Week 9 game Dan Rorabaugh, USA TODAY NETWORK - Florida Wed, October 28, 2026 at 10:06 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads A fascinating Florida-Georgia game awaits this weekend away from its usual fighting ground. With stadium renovations taking place in Jacksonville , the rivalry will be played in Atlanta this year. Both teams enter the game ranked for the first time since 2020, which is also the last time the Gators won it. UF (5-2, 3-2 in SEC) comes in hot after its second win over a top-10 team this season, a 27-24 victory at Texas . Backup quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. impressed with two touchdown passes and the game-sealing run, raising questions over whether he or Aaron Philo will get the start this week. Georgia (6-1, 4-1) fell from the ranks of the unbeaten two weeks ago when Byrum Brown spurred a late drive that led to Auburn's unbelievable 27-24 in Athens. Gunner Stockton threw for 272 yards and two score but also tossed a pair of interceptions, the second straight game in which he matched his TD and INT numbers. Buy Florida vs. Georgia football tickets Here's when the Gators and Bulldogs square off this week. Florida football schedule: UF's next game What time is UF vs UGA? The Gators and Bulldogs kick off at 3:30 p.m. on Saturday at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta. Florida vs Georgia prediction The Bulldogs have looked like the best team in the SEC all year and have numbers to show it: They rank first in the conference in both scoring offense (43 points per game) and defense (15.9 ppg). The obvious mismatch in this game comes through the air. UGA has a top-30 passing offense that has eight players with at least 100 yards receiving. UF fields a bottom-20 pass defense that allowed two straight embarrassing losses before the big Texas win. Florida has been able to counteract its deficiencies by getting to the quarterback, tying Georgia for third in the SEC with 22 sacks. UGA has protected Stockton well, though, allowing just eight sacks all year. The Gators' other big strength — Jadan Baugh and their 30th-ranked rushing attack — can also be undone by the Dawgs with their No. 10 run defense. Then again, Auburn did just run for 192 yards on them a week after Alabama put up 161 on them. This projects as Florida's best chance in years to unseat their rivals, but this being an unofficial road game might prove to be the difference. The Georgia-Florida game will be televised on ABC. Georgia is favored by almost two touchdowns against Florida . Both teams are coming off bye weeks and are looking to stay in the College Football Playoff and SEC championship hunt. The Bulldogs have won five straight games in the series, but looked far from invincible in their 27-24 home loss to the Auburn Tigers before their bye week. Florida notched a major 27-24 road upset win over the Texas Longhorns in their last outing. Both of Florida's top two quarterbacks Tramell Jones and Aaron Philo are questionable to play, so the Gators do have a major injury question entering the Georgia game. It could be some gamesmanship from Florida, but if either Philo or Jones is good to play, then Florida will be in good hands. "I have a lot of respect for this team (Florida)," Georgia coach Kirby Smart said. "Coach (Jon) Sumrall has done a great job of putting a lot of energy into the program and a lot of physicality into the program. They play really hard. When you turn on the tape, you see the physicality they play with on both sides of the ball. I have a ton of respect for both coordinators." Will Georgia beat Florida? ESPN's prediction Michai Boireau of the Florida Gators celebrates after a play against the Georgia Bulldogs Georgia is a 12-point favorite against Florida. ESPN's matchup predictor, which factors how teams have performed, football power index (FPI) and other important data, gives Georgia a 82.1% chance to defeat Florida. The Gators have just a 17.9% chance of pulling off the upset against Georgia. Seven of nine experts back Kirby Smart's team to cover, while two believe that the Gators can keep it close. Predicting the SEC has been especially difficult this season as six ranked teams suffered upset losses to unranked or lower-ranked opponents in the last two weeks alone. Georgia has won five consecutive meetings with rival Florida and eight of the past nine; seven of those victories were by two or more touchdowns. The Bulldogs are coming off a home loss to Auburn , while Florida upset Texas on the road and both teams enter Saturday off a bye week. Buster Faulkner and the Gators' offense must establish the run early and find plenty of opportunities to get Doak Walker Award hopeful Jadan Baugh involved. On the defensive side of the ball, Brad White and company must dial up the same blitz packages that helped Florida sack Manning five times and force two fumbles in the upset win. "Georgia is a double-digit favorite, but there was plenty of doubt cast on the Bulldogs last time out in a shocking home loss to Auburn. Florida, meanwhile, has epitomized the SEC with an up-and-down season. Blow out Ole Miss, get destroyed by Missouri and South Carolina, then win at Texas," wrote sports betting editor Dan Santoromita. away.headline: Florida faces Georgia with questions at quarterback
away.blurb: The answer might be a little more complicated than Florida originally anticipated. On Wednesday night, as the SEC does weekly, its teams released their first injury reports for the coming weekend. The usual suspects found their way onto Florida’s report — the most notable update entering the week: receiver Vernell Brown III is probable, despite not playing since Florida was 4-0 after a win over No. 4 Ole Miss. What wasn’t expected was that Florida’s quarterbacks would be on the report. Plural. Both questionable. At risk of going full-blown football cliché, establishing the run will prove critical for Florida … and it won’t get any easier with questions behind center. Despite the uncertainty, Florida’s staff is working to make this week seem like any other. Playing a dominant rival who has won nine of your last 10 meetings, with limited certainty about who will be quarterbacking your team, is far from typical. As in the first month of the season, Aaron Philo started for Florida against South Carolina early this month. But he injured his throwing shoulder in a rattling 38-19 defeat to a team that was previously winless in the SEC. A week later, that meant Tramell Jones Jr. took the reins. The pair had previously engaged in a quarterback duel that lasted well into fall camp, so Florida remained confident in its backup. However, a 27-24 upset of No. 9 Texas — with Jones distributing the ball well, throwing two touchdowns and committing no turnovers — wasn’t the Gators’ expected turning point. The performance left No. 17 Florida (5-2, 3-2 Southeastern Conference) with one of sports’ longest-held debates as it heads to Atlanta to face No. 3 Georgia (6-1, 4-1 SEC) on Saturday. One quarterback started for the first month of the season, managing an offense ranking in the top four nationally in scoring at more than 50 points per game. He also presided over losses to Missouri and South Carolina with a combined 84-36 scoring differential. The backup looked functional, if not better, in his lone start against a top-10 foe, but the sample size remains small. “The offense doesn’t change really with one or the other,” Florida coach Jon Sumrall said. “I do think, for us, it’s nice because we don’t drastically have to change who we are. We may lean into one guy doing certain things a little differently than the other, but it doesn’t, like all of a sudden, completely give us a different type of team.” Having neither guy, though, would pose a considerable problem. Not to mention, Florida hasn’t tallied more than 100 rushing yards against Georgia since 2015, back when Kelvin Taylor was running wild. But for the first month of this fall, Florida operated one of the best rushing attacks in the country. Jadan Baugh bulldozed 600 yards in four games, 11 touchdowns to boot. Since the turn of the month, though, SEC squads have contained him. He hasn’t run for more than 100 yards in his past three games, though his 91 against Texas suggests he might be turning a corner. Geo

away.blurb: News Sports Opinion Guardian Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL Florida football injury update | Two QBs listed as questionable for Georgia Kevin Brockway Gainesville Sun Updated Oct. 28, 2026, 8:56 p.m. ET Florida football made its quarterback situation even more cloudy heading into its matchup against rival Georgia in Atlanta. The top two Florida Gators quarterbacks on the depth chart − Aaron Philio and Tramell Jones Jr.−are both listed as questionable for UF's showdown with the Bulldogs. Philo, who started UF's first six games for the Gators , sat out Florida 's game against Texas on October 17 with a shoulder injury. Jones, who led UF to an upset win over the Longhorns by passing for 155 yards and 2 TDs, is dealing with an undisclosed injury. "He’s got a couple of bumps and bruises, too, now," Sumrall said. "And he had, you know, pulled the guy fresh out of that garage and he goes and plays, and he got a couple fender-benders. So, there's some bumps and bruises he's dealing with that are new. I noticed it last week." Also on the availability report, inside linebacker Jaden Robinson and wide receiver Bailey Stockton are listed as doubtful for UF, while running back Duke Clark has been upgraded to questionable. Wide receiver Vernell Brown III, who has missed UF's last three games with a knee strain, is listed as probable. For Georgia, wide receiver Thomas Blackshear, outside linebacker Amaris Williams and safety Tyriq Green have been ruled out. Preseason All-SEC safety KJ Bolden is listed as questionable, along with running back Chauncey Bowens and wide receiver Isiah Canon. home.headline: Georgia’s new practice routine has made two Bulldogs’ injury status unknown
home.source: Dawn of the Dawg on MSN
home.blurb: Kirby Smart detailed on Monday how Georgia handled their bye week differently this season. In the past they have continued to practice like normal with limited time off, but this year they only practiced on Tuesday and Thursday and had the rest of the week off. "Really don't know on either one of them because we haven't done anything since Thursday,” Kirby Smart said via 247Sports.com . “Those guys, we had good practices all week last week, and then leading into this week, we'll find out more about where they are today and through the injury report information we have.” Smart made it clear that he is willing to sacrifice some practice time to get his team healthy. In fact, this is something that Georgia has been doing all season because they have shortened each of their practices all season by 10 or 15 minutes. The goal in this is to help Georgia stay healthier without giving up too much preparation time, and so far it has worked out alright. The hope though is that guys like Isiah Canion and KJ Bolden could use this extra time off this week to get healthy so they can make their return against Florida this weekend, but Smart hasn't confirmed if they will be back yet or not. The hope is that this would help get Georgia as healthy as possible going into the rest of the season, but according to Smart on Monday it still isn't clear if wide receiver Isiah Canion or defensive back KJ Bolden will be healthy enough to play against Florida this weekend. Georgia’s new practice routine will hopefully pay off Georgia is 6-1 so they could be better off this season, but their record is still good enough to be the No. 3 team in the country. UGA has also had to deal with a handful of injuries throughout the season, but if you compare their injury report to other teams across the country they have had less injuries than others. Georgia desperately needs KJ Bolden back Georgia has only been without KJ Bolden for one game this season, and it just so happened to be their worst game of the year. UGA was without Bolden when they played Auburn two weeks ago and they were upset at home as the No. 1 team in the country. Who knows if Bolden could've changed that outcome if he was in the game, but it might not be a coincidence that Georgia's defense had their worst game of the season when he wasn't able to play. Georgia has been without Canion for longer, so they've already learned how to get by without him on offense. The same can't be said for Bolden though who is a projected first round pick at the upcoming NFL Draft this offseason. If Georgia wants their best shot at avoiding another upset they need Bolden back in the lineup to help slow down a Florida offense who is capable of scoring a lot of points. picks.headline: Previewing Northwestern's Upcoming Matchup Against Oregon as They Prepare to Face Another Tough Test on the Road
picks.blurb: Previewing Northwestern's Upcoming Matchup Against Oregon as They Prepare to Face Another Tough Test on the Road Skip to main content SI.COM Olympic Sports More from Northwestern Wildcats On SI FOOTBALL The Wildcats hit the road once again, this time traveling west to Eugene, Oregon, for a Big Ten showdown against the Oregon Ducks on Saturday at 2:30 p.m. CT. Oregon enters Saturday’s matchup looking to bounce back following a 21-10 loss to Illinois. The Ducks have been without starting quarterback Dante Moore for the past three games, and recent reports indicate he is unlikely to return this season after suffering a concussion earlier this year against USC. Oregon now sits at 10th in the conference with a 4-3 overall record this season. Meanwhile, the Wildcats enter Saturday’s matchup fresh off a commanding 42-14 home victory over Rutgers, a win that propelled Northwestern to No. 20 in the AP Poll. A familiar face will return to Eugene this weekend, as former Oregon head coach Chip Kelly will take on the Ducks, this time as the Wildcats’ offensive coordinator. Under Kelly’s leadership, Northwestern’s offense has emerged as one of the best in the Big Ten this season, ranking third in the conference in total yards and points per game and second in rushing yards per game. The Wildcats head to Eugene looking to build on their success on both sides of the ball and extend their four-game winning streak. A major contributor to Northwestern’s offensive success this season has been quarterback Aidan Chiles, this week’s Big Ten Offensive Player of the Week, who has thrown for over 1,600 yards and 12 touchdowns, while recording just one interception. Chiles was dominant last time out against Rutgers, throwing for 219 yards and passing for three touchdowns, while rushing for 83 yards and two touchdowns. Oct 24, 2026; Evanston, Illinois, USA; Northwestern Wildcats quarterback Aidan Chiles (0) runs with the ball against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights during the first half at New Ryan Field. Credit: David Banks- | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Alongside Chiles, wide receiver Griffin Wilde has been another standout for David Braun’s squad, recording 39 receptions for 615 yards and four touchdowns this season. Alongside Chiles, wide receiver Griffin Wilde has been another standout for David Braun’s squad, recording 39 receptions for 615 yards and four touchdowns this season. Northwestern’s rushing attack has also been a major part of its offensive success, led by the dynamic running back duo of Caleb Komolafe and Joseph Himon II, who have combined for over 900 rushing yards this season. Komolafe delivered an especially impressive performance against Rutgers, rushing for 150 yards and a touchdown in the Wildcats’ convincing victory. Defensively, Northwestern has remained stout this season, spearheaded by defensive back Robert Fitzgerald and line backer Braydon Brus. Despite missing the last two games due to injury, Fitzgerald has recorded 49 tackles and two interceptions this season. The defensive back leads the Big Ten in tackles per game with nine, followed closely by Brus in second with 8.9. Brus leads the defensive unit with 62 tackles and has also notched an interception and fumble recovery this season. Despite Dante Moore’s potential absence the rest of the season, Northwestern will still face a tough challenge on the road against a talented Oregon team. Quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas have shared playing time the past three games for the Ducks. Raiola struggled in last weekend’s loss to Illinois, completing 27 of 41 passes for 246 yards, as the defeat dealt a major blow to Oregon’s hopes of reaching the College Football Playoff for a third consecutive season. Mehringer had been promoted to the role at the start of the season after Will Stein departed to become the head coach at Kentucky, but his tenure was ultimately short-lived. This weekend’s matchup will be just the third time that both teams will be meeting, and the first time that they will match up at Autzen Stadium. They have split results, with Oregon taking the most recent matchup last season. Stay up to date on the Wildcats by bookmarking Northwestern On SI and follow us on Twitter. What will be the final result? The Oregon Ducks and Northwestern Wildcats enter Saturday’s matchup with very different expectations than they had at the beginning of the season. Oregon was expected to compete for a College Football Playoff spot, but a disappointing season, quarterback Dante Moore’s season-ending injury, and offensive coaching changes have left the Ducks searching for answers. Northwestern, meanwhile, has emerged as one of the biggest surprises in college football, entering the matchup at 6-1 and looking to strengthen its postseason resume. Can the Wildcats take advantage of Oregon’s struggles and leave Autzen Stadium with a statement victory? Or will the Ducks’ talent advantage be enough to get them back on track? Here is how the A to Z Sports team sees Saturday’s game playing out. A to Z Sports Score Predictions Tyler Forness — A to Z Sports Florida Prediction: Northwestern 24, Oregon 14 Going into the season, projecting the Wildcats to beat the Ducks would have been a shocker. On Halloween, it won’t be a trick, but rather a Wildcat treat. What Chip Kelly has done with this offense and head coach David Braun overall has been very impressive. They aren’t just 6-1 overall this season, but rank seventh in adjusted EPA/play on offense. It’s been a wild turnaround, and even though the Ducks have a huge talent surplus, their coaching staff is not in a great place, and Dante Moore is out for the year. The Northwestern playoff push continues on after a big win Saturday. Rob Gregson — A to Z Sports Alabama Prediction: Northwestern 25, Oregon 20 The 2026 Oregon Ducks are a case study in why turnover at the coordinator positions is problematic. That, and why if you can go to the NFL and be a high first-rounder, you should. The loss of Dante Moore for the season underscores what has been a messy situation from start to finish on offense this season. Will Stein has the Wildcats thriving in Kentucky, and that loss is felt in a major way. But the defense hasn’t been much better. Now, a Northwestern squad that is willing to run the ball at will is heading to Oregon, and I think they will challenge the physicality of the Ducks in a major way. Oregon doesn’t have the firepower to score, and it will be a massive win for Northwestern. Craig Smith — A to Z Sports Miami Prediction: Northwestern 23, Oregon 19 Boy, how the perception of this game has changed since Labor Day weekend. Oregon’s playoff goose is cooked at 4-3 after losses to Oklahoma State, UCLA, and Illinois. Dante Moore is done for the season. Offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer was fired after the loss to the Illini. In other words, things are a mess, particularly on the offensive side of the ball. This one stays close at Autzen Stadium, as the Ducks move the ball relatively well early on. But Northwestern, while allowing 364.6 yards per game, has been very good at keeping the point total lower, ranking 22nd nationally at 16.6 points per game. The Wildcats force some early field goals, and their ground game, paced by Caleb Komolafe, takes over the second half as the Wildcats get out of town at 7-1 and firmly in the Big Ten and playoff races. Justin Churchill — A to Z Sports Oklahoma Prediction: Oregon 20, Northwestern 17 Oregon is favored in this matchup currently by a field goal. And I have them winning by just that. Northwestern is a good team, and their story is amazing. But I think Oregon’s overall talent and coaching advantage in this one is just too good. Northwestern does have a +9 turnover margin. They force them, and they don’t commit them. Oregon cannot say the same. They have also scored on 96% of their red zone opportunities this year, which is extremely good. So, I can see why that would be enticing. But this Oregon roster is just too talented to give up on yet. Ryan Roberts — A to Z Sports Notre Dame Prediction: Oregon 21, Northwestern 20 Northwestern has earned plenty of respect with its performance this season, but I’m still leaning toward Oregon to find a way to win at home. The Ducks have endured a difficult stretch, and losing Dante Moore for the season makes an already challenging situation even more complicated. Still, the talent on this roster is difficult to overlook, particularly in a game that could come down to one or two critical possessions. Northwestern’s ability to run the football and protect the ball makes the Wildcats a dangerous opponent, especially against an Oregon team that has struggled to find consistency. However, I expect the Ducks to make just enough plays offensively to survive a tight finish. Northwestern has a legitimate opportunity to pull off the upset, but I’m giving Oregon the narrow edge at Autzen Stadium. Consensus: Can Northwestern Finish the Upset? The A to Z Sports predictions lean heavily toward Northwestern, with four of the five analysts picking the Wildcats to win. The common theme is Oregon’s offensive instability following Dante Moore’s season-ending injury and the coaching changes that have contributed to an uneven campaign. Northwestern’s ability to run the football, limit opponents’ scoring, and capitalize on mistakes gives the Wildcats a path to a major road victory. Justin Churchill and I are the exceptions, backing Oregon to lean on its roster talent and home-field advantage. Both expect a close game, and I am predicting a one-point Ducks victory. Regardless of the final score, Northwestern has an opportunity to turn an impressive start into a season-defining result. Oregon, meanwhile, needs to show that its talent can overcome the problems that have derailed its season. If the Wildcats establish the run and force Oregon into uncomfortable passing situations, an upset in Eugene could be very much in play. Kelly’s return falls on the anniversary of a memorable Halloween win. Oregon’s last home game on Halloween was in 2009, when Kelly’s Ducks beat USC 47-20 at Autzen Stadium. Moore suffered a concussion against USC on Sept. 26 and has missed the Ducks’ last three games. Ducks coach Dan Lanning said the decision is out of Moore’s hands and that the quarterback would be playing if he could. “I think if it was up to Dante in any shape, way, he would want to be out there playing for the guys,” Lanning said. “But unfortunately, it’s not really up to Dante. It’s not really up to me.” “Yeah, it’s tough, man. It’s tough,” Lanning continued. “You never step out on the football field in the middle of a game playing and then anticipate that you’re not going to get the opportunity to be able to continue to do that right now in this season and the way it is. away.headline: Northwestern Football Returns Home to Host Rutgers on Saturday
away.blurb: Limited Edition Stadium Prints Opens in a new window LAST TIME OUT On Saturday, Oct. 17, the Wildcats (5-1, 2-1 Big Ten) notched a 24-21 comeback victory over Michigan State at Spartan Stadium. Fourth-year kicker Jackson Kleather drilled a 34-yard field goal with two seconds remaining to claim the victory, Northwestern’s first game-winning play in the final five seconds of regulation since at least 2002. The win marked the Wildcats’ first time claiming a road contest after trailing by 8+ points in the fourth quarter since defeating Notre Dame in 2014 and the first time winning a game as a ranked team since the 2021 Citrus Bowl. Braden Turner : Turner made his return from injury against the Spartans, totaling five tackles, one tackle for loss and one pass breakup. The fifth-year defensive back has a 79.1 PFF defensive grade (11th among Big Ten defensive backs), 88.8 run defense grade (2nd), and 84.8 tackling grade (10th). Through three games this year, Turner has 20 tackles, three pass breakups, two tackles for loss and an interception. “The thing that I appreciate about this group is I don’t think they’re ever going to feel like they’re a finished product. There’s always going to be areas where we can grow. There’s always going to be areas from us as a coaching staff that we’re evaluating where we need to be better. … It’s easy for me to stand up here and identify the issues, but how are we going to attack those issues? What’s the ‘how’ we’re going to get that fixed? The fun part about playing in the Big Ten is just when you put one fire out and you make one fix, something else can pop up. That’s why our preparation and practice matters so much, but excited for this group to really attack that opportunity this weekend.” Javascript is required. away.headline: See who won't play for Oregon football against Northwestern
away.blurb: All three receivers missed last week's loss to Illinois for undisclosed reasons. It was the second-straight absence from the lineup for Stewart, who had been the Ducks ' leading receiver before sitting out. There were no surprises Wednesday. The seven players listed as out for Saturday's game were previously announced as injured. That includes quarterback Dante Moore, whose concussion against USC on Sept. 26 appears to be season-ending as coach Dan Lanning said Monday that he didn't anticipate Moore's return in 2026. The others listed as out were receiver Jeremiah McClellan (foot), safety Aaron Flowers (shoulder), offensive linemen Trent Ferguson (knee) and Dave Iuli (undisclosed), linebacker Brayden Platt (undisclosed) and defensive lineman Matt Johnson (undisclosed). Freshman reserve offensive lineman Immanuel Iheanacho, who was listed as out against Illinois, is now listed as questionable. Tony Cumberland – The four-star freshman defensive tackle from Eugene's Willamette High School was injured in an offseason car accident and remains out. "It's a work in progress with him," Oregon defensive line coach Tony Tuioti said Aug. 17. "I don't think it's going to be anything that we'll be able to see him soon. But he's made so much progress. I think the thing that's most important is that we have him with us and just having him in the room brings a smile to all our faces." Trent Ferguson – The junior left guard is out for the season with a knee injury suffered against Oklahoma State Sept. 12 during his first career start. Aaron Flowers – The starting safety is out for "the foreseeable future" after having surgery on his shoulder, Lanning said Oct. 14. He left the game against USC on Sept. 26 and hasn't played since.
