Who: South Carolina (4-3, 2-3 SEC) vs. Oklahoma (4-3, 2-3 SEC) When: Saturday, Oct. 31 at 4:15 p.m. Where : Memorial Stadium in Norman, Oklahoma Watch: SEC Network Stream: ESPN app or ESPN.com Broadcast crew: Taylor Zarzour, Gene Chizik, Michella Chester Local radio crew: Todd Ellis, Tommy Suggs, Chet Tucker Satellite radio: Sirius XM Channel 176 or 229 (953 on app) Series history: Tied 1-1 (Oklahoma won last matchup in 2025) South Carolina vs. Oklahoma betting odds Despite pulling off back-to-back ranked upsets, and being favored over then-No. 11 Tennessee last week, South Carolina is an underdog this week. Oklahoma opened as a 5.5-point favorite, according to the VegasInsider consensus . That line has since moved a bit and the Sooners are now favored by 4.5 points by major sportsbooks such as FanDuel and DraftKings. South Carolina is 3-4 against the spread this year. ESPN Analytics also favors the Sooners. ESPN gives South Carolina a 36.1% chance of winning the game. Injury updates South Carolina had seven players listed on the official SEC injury report released Wednesday night. WR Jayden Sellers, edge rusher Kobby Sakyi-Prah, OL Josian Thompson, OL Dayne Arnett and OL Seth Smith are all listed as out. Sellers and Thompson are both out for the year. DB Quay'sheed Scott and RB Jawarn Howell are both listed as doubtful. Scott has missed the last two games. Howell was out last week vs. Tennessee. The SEC injury report will be updated on Thursday, Friday and 90 minutes before kickoff on Saturday. Weather forecast for the game in Norman If you're making the trip to Oklahoma this weekend, be sure to pack an umbrella and a jacket. Temperatures aren't expected to surpass 64 degrees and will dip into the mid-50s. There will be thick cloud cover with a touch of rain, per Accuweather's 10-day forecast. There's a 55% chance of rain all day Saturday for the Norman area. Top storylines Three's a streak: A win over Oklahoma on Saturday would give South Carolina its third straight win. The Gamecocks haven't won three consecutive SEC games since they ended the 2024 season with four straight SEC wins. That six-game winning streak to close out the 2024 season was also the last time the Gamecocks won three games in a row. Should USC beat Oklahoma, it would get the Gamecocks' SEC record back to .500. Sellers needs help in the run game: Make no mistake, South Carolina still has the No. 1 rushing offense in the SEC. The Gamecocks are averaging 218 yards per game, but things haven't looked perfect in recent weeks. Anyone not named LaNorris Sellers has had trouble consistently running the ball for South Carolina. Sellers has accounted for 313 of the 480 rushing yards the Gamecocks have compiled in the last three games. That's certainly good, but USC's running backs need to get going so all the pressure isn't on Sellers' legs down the stretch. Ranking on the horizon? South Carolina received votes in both the Associated Press Top 25 and USA Today Coaches Poll this week after beating Tennessee. USC received 12 votes from the coaches and eight votes from the media. Will a win over Oklahoma be enough to catapult USC into the national rankings for the first time since September 2025? Only time will tell. South Carolina and Oklahoma players to watch South Carolina K Malik Orsan: The sophomore was South Carolina's savior last week. Orsan drilled a 48-yard field goal to help the Gamecocks beat then-No. 11 Tennessee 27-24 as the clock expired. The Southeast Missouri State transfer wasn't necessarily considered to be the top kicker on the roster during USC's kicking competition this offseason. But he's quickly proven why he won the starting job by going 10 for 12 on field goal attempts and 22 for 22 on extra-point attempts this season. South Carolina OL Nolan Hay: The fifth-year offensive lineman was named the Outland Trophy National Player of the Week on Tuesday by the Football Writers Association of America. Hay has been one of the best offensive linemen for the Gamecocks this year. He typically starts at guard but has played some center in Carter Miller's absence because of injury. Hay's Pro Football Focus blocking grade is one of the best on the team. Oklahoma QB John Mateer: There was some buzz around Mateer's name this offseason, but he's found himself in a bit of a rut in 2026. Mateer has thrown for 1,591 yards and 11 touchdowns but has also thrown seven interceptions. He's got a strong arm and is capable of using his legs in the ground game, but has been generally turnover-prone this season. Oklahoma WR Isaiah Sategna III: Sategna was an All-SEC player last year after finishing with 965 receiving yards. The fifth-year student has been Mateer's favorite target in 2026. Sategna leads Oklahoma with 41 catches and 578 yards.

away.headline: Oklahoma vs. South Carolina: Initial injury report for Week 9
away.blurb: On offense, key players like Ryan Fodje and Eddy Pierre-Louis aren't close to returning and were ruled out for this week. However, guard Heath Ozaeta could make his first appearance since the win over Texas. Ozaeta was listed as probable. If he's able to play, that provides Oklahoma a valuable piece to their interior offensive line rotation. If he's able to play, it's likely Ozaeta slides back into the starting lineup, but could platoon with Peyton Joseph, who has had some ups and downs for the Sooners over the last two weeks. It also looks like running back Xavier Robinson could be available this week. The Carl Albert product hasn't played since the Week 4 loss to Georgia and saw fewer than 10 snaps in back-to-back weeks before suffering a calf strain. He'll battle with Jonathan Hatton for the third running back carries as Lloyd Avant and Tory Blaylock have established themselves as the Sooners' 1-2 punch in the running back rotation. Defensively, the Oklahoma Sooners have big questions. Rotational linebacker Cole Sullivan was ruled out for this week. Safety Peyton Bowen and cornerback Eli Bowen are both questionable for Week 9. Both Bowens are key pieces to the Sooners' defense, and against a good South Carolina passing attack, Peyton's presence is critical. He's one of the best safeties in college football. If he can't play, it'll be Omarion Robinson and Michael Boganowski starting at the safety spots, and potentially Reggie Powers mixing into the rotation. If Eli is out, Trystan Haynes would likely get another start. He's been solid since entering the starting lineup against the Texas Longhorns and would need to be at his best this week if called upon to start. Injuries have once again been a key storyline for the Sooners in the 2026 season. If the key players listed as questionable and probable can be available for this week, it would give the Sooners a boost on both sides of the football. home.headline: Kamario Taylor injury update: Mississippi State QB latest status vs Oklahoma
home.blurb: Mississippi State's offense looked out of sorts last week against LSU without Kamario Taylor, as the Bulldogs' offense was shut out for the first time in six seasons. Initial signs from Wednesday's SEC player availability report signaled ... maybe. Taylor remained listed as questionable for the Bulldogs' SEC matchup against the Sooners, according to Friday's player availability report. as he continues to recover from an undisclosed injury. Pete Thamel reported on Oct. 24 , however, Taylor will in fact be playing through his malady against the Sooners. Taylor was listed as questionable on Mississippi State's initial SEC player availability report on Wednesday for Saturday's game vs. Oklahoma. He remained questionable on Friday, but according to Pete Thamel, he will play against Oklahoma. Taylor was downgraded to out ahead of last Saturday's game against LSU due to an undisclosed injury. Before kickoff, he was seen wearing street clothes and a walking boot on the sideline. Be sure to check out USA TODAY Sports' new College Football Unfiltered podcast , hosted by USA TODAY Sports columnist Blake Toppmeyer. You can stream on YouTube or download via Apple podcasts and Spotify . Will the Bulldogs get some help with their star quarterback back under center in Week 8 against Oklahoma? BOWL PREDICTIONS: Week 7 upsets impact college football bowl projections with CFP field shuffling From NFL plays to college sports scores, all the top sports news you need to know every day. Taylor has been one of the top quarterbacks in the SEC this season, though his hot start cooled off just before exiting Mississippi State's loss to Alabama on Oct. 3 with an injury. He ranks sixth in the SEC in passing yards (1,450) and leads the conference in touchdown passes (17). The Bulldogs host the Sooners at 3:30 p.m. ET on Saturday at Davis Wade Stadium in Starkville, Mississippi. "The injury report will continue to speak to that," Lebby said on Oct. 19. "I talked about it in the post-game (news conference vs LSU). He didn't wake up yesterday morning and was healed. It's going to be day-to-day. He's got a lot of work to do, but we'll see where we end up." The first-year starting quarterback exited the Bulldogs' Week 5 game vs. Alabama in the fourth quarter with an apparent injury. He was seen on the ESPN broadcast first walking into the locker room with members of Mississippi State's medical staff. As noted by the Clarion Ledger — part of the USA TODAY Network — Taylor was seen wearing a boot on his right ankle for the remainder of the frame once he returned to the sidelines. Lebby noted in his postgame news conference after the 56-23 loss to Alabama that Taylor had been dealing with a prior injury heading into the game. What injury does Kamario Taylor have? Taylor is dealing with an undisclosed lower-body injury. home.headline: Key Sooners on offense trending toward playing vs. Mississippi State
home.blurb: The Oklahoma Sooners saw some positive movement in the SEC's Thursday evening availability report . Wide receiver Parker Livingstone and running back Tory Blaylock were moved to probable ahead of Saturday's matchup with Mississippi State . Livingstone missed the Kentucky game and will likely need to play a big role for the Sooners with Elijah Thomas still questionable on Thursday night. If Thomas isn't able to go, that puts Manny Choice getting his second straight start on the outside along with Isaiah Sategna in the slot. Livingstone would have a great shot to start on the outside in three-wide receiver sets. All eyes are still on left tackle Michael Fasusi, who remained questionable Thursday night. With Ryan Fodje out, it's critical that Fasusi plays this week against Mississippi State. If he can't go, look for Peyton Joseph to get the start at left tackle. But that would leave a whole at right guard, unless Heath Ozaeta, who is also questionable, can play. Hoping to make his return is cornerback Eli Bowen. Bowen has been out since a practice injury suffered before the Texas game. But Oklahoma could use his speed and coverage ability as the Sooners get set to take on a speedy Bulldogs wide receiver group. Blaylock carried the ball seven times for 23 yards and ran with patience and burst. It was the best he has looked since the College Football Playoff loss to Alabama. Platooning him with Lloyd Avant and Jonathan Hatton helped create a more effective running game than we've had this season. Now the running back room has to build on it. For the Mississippi State Bulldogs , there was no movement on star quarterback Kamario Taylor and running back Fluff Bothwell. Both players missed Mississippi State 31-0 shutout at the hands of the LSU Tigers in Week 7. If they can't play, that significantly increases Oklahoma's chances of earning a win on the road this week. If they do play, the Sooners offense will be under pressure to score to keep pace with Jeff Lebby's offense in Starkville. Here's a look at the Thursday night availability report. picks.headline: Clemson Tigers vs Florida State Seminoles Preview & Start Time — October 31, 2026 | SI
ESPN predicts the winner of Clemson football vs. Florida State
picks.blurb: Clemson (4-3, 3-2 ACC) is coming off a last-minute 20-16 loss to the Virginia Tech Hokies at Memorial Stadium. The Tigers led for much of the second half, but Hokies quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer led his team on an 11-play, 69-yard drive for the game-winning score with 1:44 to play. Grunkmeyer's 5-yard touchdown pass to tight end Luke Reynolds on fourth-and-1 gave Virginia Tech its first win over Clemson in 19 years and dropped the Tigers to 2-8 in their last 10 home games against Power Four opponents. The offense struggled once again, netting only 288 total yards and going 3 of 14 on third downs. Freshman QB Tait Reynolds completed 20 of his 26 passes, but his average completion went for only 5.9 yards. The Tigers rank dead last in the ACC and just 115th nationally in total offense with 333.1 yards per game. Clemson will face a Florida State (3-4, 1-3) team fresh off a bye, and one that should be playing with plenty of confidence. Mike Norvell's Seminoles took the top-ranked Miami Hurricanes into double overtime before falling 43-35 at Hard Rock Stadium on Oct. 17. Fifth-year senior Ashton Daniels leads the Seminoles' passing attack and has 1,618 yards and 12 touchdowns to eight interceptions in seven games this season. Daniels threw four touchdown passes and rushed for another score in FSU's loss to Miami in Week 7. Clemson has won nine of the last 10 meetings against Florida State dating back to 2015. Will the Tigers' run of dominance in the rivalry continue or end Saturday in Tallahassee? Will Clemson football beat Florida State? ESPN's prediction Oddsmakers have Florida State as a 6.5-point favorite over Clemson, but as always, ESPN Analytics has its own odds for Saturday's game. ESPN's matchup predictor , which offers a prediction model based on its college football power index and other variables, doesn't favor the Tigers, either. It gives Florida State a 71.9% chance to win and Clemson a 28.1% chance. The Tigers are 51st nationally in ESPN's FPI with a 5.8 rating, which ranks 11th among the 17 ACC teams. Florida State has a 10.1 FPI rating that's 37th nationally. The Tigers are one spot ahead of Kansas State (5.7) and one spot below Virginia (6.0). Clemson football odds of reaching bowl game after brutal Week 7 loss to Virginia Tech In ESPN's FPI entering Week 8, Clemson's chances of reaching six wins to qualify for a bowl game stand at 78.1%, down from 88.4% prior to its loss to Virginia Tech. Clemson's chances of winning its final five games are just 2.1%, according to ESPN's FPI. ESPN explains: "The Football Power Index (FPI) is a measure of team strength that is meant to be the best predictor of a team's performance going forward for the rest of the season. FPI represents how many points above or below average a team is. Projected results are based on 20,000 simulations of the rest of the season using FPI, results to date, and the remaining schedule. Ratings and projections update daily. FPI data from seasons prior to 2019 may not be complete." away.blurb: One talking point going into the game, and really a talking point each week, is injuries and how they are going to affect depth charts for both teams. On Wednesday, the initial injury report for the game was released, and Virginia Tech cornerback Cam Chadwick was listed as questionable. On Thursday, another name was dropped, and the UConn transfer was off the list, which is a good sign. However, a couple of names still popped up for the Hokies who sound like they'll be game-time decisions at best. Offensive lineman Montavious Cunningham and cornerback Thomas Williams were both listed as questionable. As far as Clemson goes, defensive tackle Vic Burley is listed as questionable. When Franklin was hired by Virginia Tech, you knew that attendance at games was not going to be an issue with the Hokies' fans. Heck, they came out in droves last season, with a dismal season that saw Brent Pry fired after a Week 3 loss at home to Old Dominion. There are still two more home games remaining on the slate for Franklin and his team this season, and it was announced that those two final games will be played in front of a full house. The game on Nov. 14 against Stanford was already sold out, but now Virginia Tech has officially sold out the Commonwealth Clash against Virginia on Nov. 28. To think, Virginia Tech didn't even need to have two-for-one promos to get it sold out in late November. This is expected to be one of the better Commonwealth Clashes in some time. The Hokies will be looking to become bowl-eligible with a win after winning five of their first seven games, while the Tigers come in at 4-2 in a battle in primetime on ESPN between a pair of two-loss ACC teams in late October. Freshman Benjamin Eziuka played nearly 50 snaps against the Yellow Jackets last weekend and will be ready to go this weekend if Cunningham can't go again. It'll be a tough environment for Eziuka to play at Clemson, but Franklin doesn't appear to be nervous about putting him in. "He's dense; he's powerful in the weight room, and he's super trustworthy," Franklin said at his Wednesday media availability . "Obviously, everybody uses that quote: 'Do your job.' He's that guy. away.headline: FSU football wary of Clemson star Ashton Hampton in personal homecoming
away.blurb: "He's really long, he's fast, really athletic, really fluid in his movements and can get in and out of breaks really well. I'm really looking forward to going against him. It's going to present a good challenge, and I truly can't wait to face a corner of that caliber." Florida State football's Halloween weekend showdown with Clemson carries extra significance for one of the Tigers' top defensive players. Former Florida High standout Ashton Hampton returns to Tallahassee on Saturday night when Clemson visits Doak Campbell Stadium for a 7 p.m. kickoff. The junior cornerback has emerged as one of the ACC's premier defensive backs, drawing high praise from FSU coach Mike Norvel l ahead of the matchup. "I think Ashton is one of the best corners in the country," Norvell said. Hampton, a third-year junior, enters the game leading the ACC with nine pass breakups, a total tied for third nationally. He also has 25 tackles and one interception this season and is already viewed as a potential first-round NFL draft prospect when he becomes eligible. FSU wide receiver Duce Robinson knows firsthand the challenge Hampton presents. The two faced off last season, when Hampton totaled 10 tackles, including seven solo stops, and broke up two passes against the Seminoles. Robinson said Hampton's combination of size, athleticism and technique makes him one of the nation's elite cornerbacks. "We played Ashton last year, and he's a really, really big corner," Robinson said. Hampton is not the only playmaker in Clemson 's secondary. Opposite him is Elliott Washington, a Penn State transfer who leads the Tigers with three interceptions. The 5-foot-11 defensive back has added 22 tackles, four pass breakups and a forced fumble, helping anchor a secondary that has become one of Clemson's strengths. Norvell said the Tigers' defensive backfield has improved significantly and presents challenges across the board. "Washington's done a really good job coming in there," Norvell said. "The safety play is much improved from where it was maybe a year ago, and the front unit, with all the different things they do, presents a lot of challenges." With Hampton returning to his hometown and Clemson bringing one of the ACC's top defenses to Tallahassee, FSU's offense faces one of its toughest tests of the season. For the Seminoles, the challenge is clear. They must solve a talented secondary and snap a two-game skid. For Hampton, it's a chance to shine once again on the field where his football journey first captured local attention. home.blurb: Florida State coach Mike Norvell recently provided a couple of injury updates on multiple Seminoles who have missed significant time this season. Injuries have been a huge issue for the team this year for Norvell, particularly on defense, where multiple players are out for the season. Sometimes injuries can make or break a team, and so far, the Seminoles have been able to do quite a bit with multiple contributors sidelined. Norvell kicked off his injury updates portion of the press conference with a quick tidbit on linebacker Blake Nichelson, who has not played since the season opener against New Mexico State. Nichelson is nearing a return, and while the game against Clemson might still be out of reach , the linebacker should be able to return to play soon. Samuel Singleton Jr.'s return would be huge for the Florida State offense Norvell is not giving up on Singleton's return; he never ruled the running back out for the season, and he clearly still thinks there is hope for his return. It might be a delusion at this point from Norvell to avoid the reality that Florida State is in a bad spot at running back, or a future return this season might still truly be in the cards. I personally would like to think that Singleton is close to coming back, and the faster he can return, the better for Florida State. Tre Wisner is an experienced running back, but he has not been the most effective player in a short sample size this season. Aside from Wisner, there is not much of an experienced supporting cast. home.headline: Quindarrius Jones injury update: Florida State's banged-up secondary continues to take hits
home.blurb: With the game against Clemson quickly approaching for Florida State, a top defensive back has been ruled out. Starting corner Quindarrius Jones left the game against Miami in Week 7 after playing just 14 snaps. Jones had a week to recover with the bye, which brought some hope, but the defender will not be able to play against Clemson. Jones has missed two games this season now after sitting out the home game against Central Arkansas earlier in the year. Frankly, it was better for the defense to play Central Arkansas without him, so more defensive backs would be able to see the field. However, against Clemson, Florida State cannot afford to suffer another injury at an already weak position. The secondary has been torn to shreds all year, with Karson Hobbs and Jamari Howard spending the majority of the season on the injury report. Jones has missed time, freshman Jordan Crutchfield has been unavailable most of the season, and Chuck Kennon was dismissed just as he began to recover from an injury. With Jones out, two players will likely take over: Charles Lester III and Jordan Crutchfield, who will be making his return from an injury against Clemson. Lester has been the main replacement for Jones this season, playing 33 snaps against Miami after Jones left the game. Lester also replaced Jones for the game against Central Arkansas, logging 34 snaps. Jones typically plays between 45 and 55 snaps each week, with his total number of snaps played increasing as the injuries in the secondary have stacked up. Lester has been covering a good portion of the missing snaps, but against Miami, Ja'Bril Rawls played 74 out of 80 possible snaps, which is something he has done multiple times this season. Lester is more than likely going to resume the same role he has previously taken when Jones is forced to sit out, but the addition of a healthy Crutchfield gives the staff options. Fellow safety KJ Kirkland is expected to play, but has been dealing with an injury, which could create a different avenue to the field for Crutchfield. In limited playing time this season, Lester has proven to be effective at times, with eight total tackles, including three against Miami after Jones left the game. Lester has struggled at times in coverage, but his ability to recover and limit additional gains is notable. picks.headline: Miami Hurricanes at North Carolina Tar Heels game predictions: Can the Canes finally snap their ugly streak against UNC?
picks.blurb: Miami Hurricanes at North Carolina Tar Heels game predictions: Can the Canes finally snap their ugly streak against UNC? Skip to content NFL Close Menu All NFL Buffalo Bills Miami Dolphins New England Patriots New York Jets Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Pittsburgh Steelers Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Tennessee Titans Denver Broncos Kansas City Chiefs Las Vegas Raiders Los Angeles Chargers Dallas Cowboys New York Giants Philadelphia Eagles Washington Commanders Chicago Bears Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Minnesota Vikings Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers New Orleans Saints Tampa Bay Buccaneers Arizona Cardinals Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Seattle Seahawks College Football Close Menu All College Football Alabama Crimson Tide Auburn Tigers Florida Gators Georgia Bulldogs Miami Hurricanes Michigan Wolverines Notre Dame Fighting Irish Ohio State Buckeyes Oklahoma Sooners Ole Miss Rebels Penn State Nittany Lions Tennessee Volunteers Texas A&M Aggies Texas Longhorns Draft Simulator Trade Simulator CFB Playoff Predictor Toggle Mobile Navigation Home College Football The Canes finally appear to have the roster to overcome some bad history in Chapel Hill. Things have not gone well for the Miami Hurricanes when they go to Chapel Hill. The Canes have lost four of their last five matchups at UNC, and there have been some lopsided losses in that stretch. But this Miami team has an offense that has a strong argument the best in all of college football. Will the Canes come away victorious in a place that's been a house of horrors for them in recent years? Our college football writers weighed in on the game. Miami 41, UNC 24 Could this be a trap game for the Hurricanes? You can never say no with Bill Belichick on the other side, but it's highly unlikely. Miami has been phenomenal this season, with Darian Mensah taking a big step forward in Shannon Dawson's offense. He and Malachi Toney have been fantastic this season, and the only way the Tar Heels have a realistic chance to win is by forcing the Hurricanes to win with explosive plays, as their best successes have been sustaining drives, with a 99th percentile EPA/play and non-explosive EPA/play. – Tyler Forness , A to Z Sports Florida Miami 47, North Carolina 21 This is an opponent that's given Miami absolute fits, with the Heels winning five straight since Miami's last win in 2018. Even the 2017 Orange Bowl Miami team struggled in 2017 in Chapel Hill against a 2-10 UNC team. It's just how it's gone in this series for Miami. But this isn't any Miami team. History and vibes can't overcome a major talent edge that Miami holds, particularly at the quarterback position. Syracuse's Steve Angeli threw for 256 yards and two scores last week, and the Orange had two receivers with 86+ receiving yards. Darian Mensah and Malachi Toney are about to go off, and the Canes won't look back. The streak ends in emphatic fashion. – Craig Smith , A to Z Sports Miami Miami 50, North Carolina 25 Bill Belichick has already gone on record about how difficult it is to cover Miami WR Malachi Toney, but now his team is going to get an up-close and personal look at just how impossible that task is. Toney had more receiving yards at halftime last week than the entirety of the Pitt Panthers. There's a chance that happens again against North Carolina. Belichick may be one of the best defensive minds to ever grace the sport of football, but it comes down to having the horses on the field, and I think it's safe to say that his stable isn't exactly ready for Toney. Miami will roll this week as long as they don't look ahead to Notre Dame. Escaping a trap game ahead of next week is priority number one for the Hurricanes. – Rob Gregson , A to Z Sports Alabama Miami 31, North Carolina 17 Miami comes away with a 31-17 win over North Carolina, but this game should be more competitive than the final score suggests. Bill Belichick’s squad comes ready to play and does a good job hanging around through the first half, making the Hurricanes work for everything offensively. North Carolina shows some fight on both sides of the ball, and the Tar Heels do enough to keep the pressure on Miami for much of the afternoon. However, the talent gap between these two teams eventually becomes difficult to ignore. Miami has more playmakers capable of changing a game in an instant, and that difference starts to show as the second half unfolds. Quarterback Darian Mensah is the difference-maker for the Hurricanes when they need him most. With North Carolina still within striking distance, Mensah delivers a couple of explosive plays in the second half that swing the momentum and allow Miami to create some breathing room. Those plays help the Hurricanes put the game away and turn what had been a tight contest into a more comfortable victory on the scoreboard. Belichick’s team deserves credit for competing and making Miami earn the win, but the Hurricanes’ superior talent ultimately takes over down the stretch. It gets just about any player it wants, its realistic expectations are national title or bust, and it's one of the few programs that can lose its starting quarterback and still reasonably be considered the No. 1 team in the country. But now it has to go at least the next several weeks without star quarterback Julian Sayin, who injured his shoulder in the win over Indiana a few weeks ago. There's a quarterback battle to see who steps into the role as the team travels to Los Angeles to face a desperate USC team in a whole lot of trouble. The Trojans are 6-2, but they just got stuffed by Wisconsin in a punishing 24-7 loss, and with a brutal schedule to close, the Lincoln Riley hot seat is flaming. On the plus side, win, and the team is still deep in the College Football Playoff hunt. Ohio State vs USC: Quick Hits It doesn't get any easier for USC with a trip to Indiana next after a week off, and then Maryland, and it all closes at UCLA. Ohio State finishes with three of its last four games in Columbus, hosting Oregon next week. The road game is at Nebraska. This is the first time these two have met since a 24-7 Ohio State win in the 2017 Cotton Bowl. USC has won seven or the last eight in the series goning back to the 1974 Rose Bowl. It beat Washington and Penn State, but lost at home to a struggling Oregon, and couldn't get anything going against the Badgers. Ohio State isn't the Ohio State of previous seasons, but it's still good enough to beat anyone else this year. To win, the Buckeyes have to screw up, but USC doesn't take the ball away with just six turnovers forced on the season, and there's little running game to worry about. Fahey missed both of his throws against Indiana, and St. Clair has only seen the lightest of mop-up work so far. Ohio State vs USC Prediction, Betting Lines Which team has another gear? We have a number of intriguing matchups this week, and it all starts on Friday night. To kick off my Week 9 betting card, I'm looking toward a Big 12 battle between the Baylor Bears — who just fired their head coach — and the UCF Knights, who just pulled off their first-ever upset over a top-five team. On Saturday, we'll begin in Iowa City, where the Iowa Hawkeyes will look to bounce back in a trophy game against the No. 25 Wisconsin Badgers. Then, in the SEC, the No. 17 Florida Gators meet the No. 3 Georgia Bulldogs for the World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party in Atlanta. Finally, to close it all out, we'll take a look at a Big Ten tilt between the No. 2 Ohio State Buckeyes and USC Trojans. With so much to get to, let's dive into my college football picks and NCAAF predictions for the Week 9 games on Saturday, October 31. Baylor has fired head coach Dave Aranda, a move made after a critical loss to Kansas in Week 8. The former LSU defensive coordinator leaves Waco with a 40-40 overall mark, not good enough for the current administration. Former athletic director Mack Rhoades took a separation agreement in November 2025, leaving Aranda's future in doubt under new athletic director Doug McNamee. Defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman, recently brought in from Kansas State , will serve as the interim coach as Baylor looks to reach bowl season. The Baylor defense was never the issue this season, allowing an average of 16.1 points per game. The offense, under transfer quarterback DJ Lagway, has severely struggled with coordinator Jake Spavital. The Bears sit outside the top 110 in Success Rate on offense, relying on pass explosives as the only means of creating scoring opportunities. Despite the struggles as a whole, Lagway has seen improvement from his days at Florida with an increase in big-time throws and a lower turnover-worthy play rate. The Bears struggle in scoring position, averaging just 3.3 points on 50 offensive possessions inside the opponent's 40-yard line. Red-zone efficiency has been a constant failure all season, ranking 121st in touchdown percentage. Only half of the 30 possessions that made it into the red zone have resulted in a Baylor touchdown. UCF had one of the more advantageous spots of the entire college football calendar when hosting BYU , as the Cougars were coming off a program-defining win over Notre Dame . The overtime game provided all the thrills for a college football masterpiece, as the Knights took a field-storming victory with an 89% post-game win expectancy. Backup quarterback Keyone Jenkins led UCF to four methodical drives and an explosive passing attack, tossing six explosives through the air. The defense had the assignment of slowing down Heisman hopeful Bear Bachmeier , and it limited the BYU quarterback to just 37 rushing yards on 15 carries. The biggest factor was basic fundamentals, as the Knights missed just nine tackles in the game to add on a PFF tackling grade that ranks in the top 25. The Cougars' high-octane offense was limited to just a single rush explosive. It makes sense considering UCF's defense ranks 15th in Line Yards and top-40 in Rush EPA allowed. The handicap on this game forces handicappers to look beyond the advanced statistics, as the Baylor program is in flux. Klanderman isn't expected to win the job as Baylor's head coach, as McNamee has made it clear a coach with Texas roots and an offensive mindset will be the next hire. The downstream effect of the coaching search could create outside noise for coordinators and players looking for their next stop if they don't make a bowl game. Statistically, Baylor could have a hard time generating points against the UCF defense. The Bears have generated plenty of available yards to create scoring opportunities, but a rank outside the top 100 in Finishing Drives will go against a Knights defense that's 32nd in limiting opponents in scoring position. With the expectation that UCF will have a hangover from one of the most electric college football games of the season, a first-half under is the look from a statistical and spot perspective. There are also advantages for UCF in the run game against the Baylor defense. The Bears have a top-10 unit in terms of Rushing Success Rate allowed but have a mid-FBS average of 50% against teams that use inside zone. The Knights run a heavy amount of inside zone through Jenkins and running back Duke Watson . A boost could be in store if quarterback Alonza Barnett III returns from a hamstring injury. The James Madison transfer suited up for the BYU game but did not play for the fifth straight game. Any contribution from Barnett would further solidify UCF's position. The Gators remain at two losses on the season in the thick of the SEC race and a potential spot in the College Football Playoff, but a date with Georgia in the World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party comes first. The biggest takeaway from the victory over Texas came from backup quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. tossing a couple of touchdowns in a mistake-free game. The sophomore completed 22-of-35 passes while chipping in 50 rushing yards with an even split of scrambles and designed run calls. On the other side, the defense continues to rank as one of the best in the nation when creating chaos. The top-10 Havoc numbers are led by 53 tackles for loss , nine forced fumbles and 34 passes defensed. Five players on the defensive line have generated double-digit pressures, while seven different defenders have multiple pass breakups. The issue with Florida's defense is its performance close to the goal line, ranking 95th in red-zone defense. The Gators have allowed 40 opponent possessions to cross the 40-yard line and are giving up an average of 4.4 points per trip . Georgia's first loss to Auburn in nine years comes as a result of ball protection. Quarterback Gunner Stockton was responsible for two interceptions and a fumble, an uncharacteristic set of events for the senior. Up until the Alabama game in Week 6, Stockton managed to throw just six interceptions and lose three fumbles since the beginning of the 2025 season. In the past two games, the Georgia quarterback has committed two fumbles and three interceptions . There's the case that Stockton had too much of the load against Auburn, taking a critical hit in the first series of the game. Running back Chauncey Bowens has missed multiple games with injury, while Nate Frazier was ineffective coming off a rib injury, finishing with less than 20 rushing yards. The bye week should provide the best health for the offense in weeks, as head coach Kirby Smart described Bowens as day-to-day . Stockton should also be fully recovered from any shoulder or concussion symptoms. The Bulldogs defense continues to be one of the best nationally in defending the run, ranking top-25 in Rushing Success Rate allowed and Defensive Line Yards. Cornerback Ellis Robinson IV has been one of the best at shutting down wideouts all season with five pass breakups and an interception. Defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann has been excellent in disguising blitzes this season, as the highest tally of pressures this season comes from linebackers Chris Cole and Raylen Wilson. The Gators have struggled to run the ball of late, posting a Stuff Rate above the national average in the last three SEC contests against Texas, South Carolina and Missouri . Florida has three primary run concepts in the arsenal: outside zone, counter and power. The most successful and explosive of the group comes from power attempts with a heavy box, led by running back Jadan Baugh. The junior has 100 more rushing attempts than any other player on the team, running an even split of zone read and non-zone read concepts. Despite the highly successful numbers against zone read and counter, Georgia has been horrific against power concepts this season . The Bulldogs have elite numbers in Defensive Finishing Drives and red-zone prevention, ranking fifth in red-zone drives allowed. Although only 15 drives have passed the Georgia 20, the Bulldogs have allowed 14 scores, with 11 of the 15 drives resulting in a touchdown . On the other side of the ball, Georgia has been a pure zone-read team with a heavy batch of inside zone with 11 and 12 personnel. Nearly every run concept from the Bulldogs comes in well above the national average in Success Rate and EPA, but inside and outside zone read produce an explosive on one of every five attempts. Florida has been successful against outside zone but has yet to see an offense execute with two-tight end sets. Georgia should thrive in passing downs, as the Gators sit outside the top 90 in Success Rate and EPA allowed when opponents are off schedule . Florida has been putrid at keeping opponents out of scoring position and the end zone this season. On the other side, Georgia defense has been dominated by power run concepts, so Baugh should find a way to put Florida on the board. Jones is also an X-factor, as offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner will have an expanded playbook for the sophomore and starter Aaron Philo. The betting odds for the game already tell a clear story. The Ohio State Buckeyes' Week 9 matchup on the road against the USC Trojans is a big one, and the betting line already tells a story. Ohio State heads into the primetime Halloween game without quarterback Julian Sayin for the first time since 2024. Oddsmakers still have the Buckeyes as a solid road favorite in Big Ten play. At one point, this game looked even bigger on paper because USC figured to be ranked. Instead, the 5-2 Trojans are unranked after a blowout loss to Wisconsin. They're now facing a must-win situation against Ohio State if they want to reach the postseason. Ohio State is without Julian Sayin against USC For Ohio State, this game carries extra weight. Sayin suffered an injury against Indiana in the game before the bye week, and it all but knocked him out for the season. It's the first time the Buckeyes will play without him under center since 2024. Ohio State hasn't named a starting quarterback for the trip to USC. Still, everything we know points to Luke Fahey getting the nod against the Trojans. Even with a first-time starter on the road, the The Buckeyes will want to run the ball a bit more to take pressure off a new quarterback, and that's going to be vital for the offense to move consistently. Oddsmakers are siding with the Buckeyes FanDuel has Ohio State as a 6.5-point favorite on the road, with the moneyline available at -240. Despite missing their starting quarterback, the Buckeyes are just about a touchdown favorite over USC. A big reason why is the defense. Ohio State allows just 13.4 points per game, which ranks in the top 5 in the country. That unit draws a USC offense that wants to air the ball out behind quarterback Jayden Maiava. Throwing the ball is how the Trojans find their offensive success. If Ohio State can slow down Maiava, its chances of picking up another quality road win are strong. On the flip side, USC isn't that strong defensively. The Trojans' defensive line is solid and carries the unit. However, the defense ranks 76th in the country at 25 points allowed per game. That should give Fahey and the Ohio State offense a chance to settle in. It's a big game for both programs for different reasons. Ohio State can drop this one and still be in the mix for the College Football Playoff come January. A loss would knock the Trojans' playoff chances out the window. It could also spell the end of Lincoln Riley's tenure in Southern California. Pretty large Big Ten implications are on the line, and oddsmakers are clearly siding with the Buckeyes on the road. Saturday night will show whether Ohio State can pass its first test without Sayin. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. away.headline: What is the status of Ohio State's Kenyatta Jackson Jr., Jay Timmons?
away.blurb: "Last week was a great opportunity to get a bunch of guys some rest," Ohio State coach Ryan Day said. "We'll see how this week goes. ... [Most] will probably go through the rest of the week, and as we get closer to the game, we'll get an idea." Jackson was helped to the medical tent by two Ohio State athletic trainers with 11:55 remaining in the Buckeyes ' 19-15 road win on Oct. 17. He returned for the Hoosiers' final drive but then had to be helped by defensive tackle Eddrick Houston and a trainer going back to the locker room. The fifth-year defender provides crucial experience, as he's the only remaining Ohio State defensive lineman who appeared in all 16 games during the 2024 national championship run. Along with leading the Buckeyes in sacks this season (3), Jackson has played 320 snaps, according to PFF – 63 more than any other Ohio State defensive lineman. Of Jackson's 22 tackles, seven came against the Hoosiers, marking his career high. Timmons also had a career game in Bloomington, recording seven tackles, two pass breakups and a forced fumble, before being sidelined for Ohio State's final defensive drives. The freshman was dealing with an unspecified injury leading up to the Indiana game, missing the previous two matchups. In his first four Ohio State games, Timmons logged nine tackles, four pass breakups and a forced fumble in the opening drive against Texas. He was initially hurt in the third quarter against Illinois on Sept. 26. No. 2 Ohio State will travel to face No. 15 Southern California on Oct. 31.

away.blurb: News Sports Business Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL DB Jay Timmons among Ohio State starters questionable for USC game Brianna Mac Kay Columbus Dispatch Oct. 28, 2026, 8:56 p.m. ET Along with quarterback Julian Sayin and running back Ja'Kobi Jackson , Ohio State football could be without two more starters for the USC game on Oct. 31. Ohio State nickel back Jay Timmons and wide receiver Brandon Inniss are listed as questionable on the Buckeyes ' initial availability report, released by the Big Ten three days before the game. Sayin and Jackson are the only starters among seven Buckeyes already ruled out. Freshman wide receiver Brock Boyd is also listed as questionable. Sayin and Jackson were expected to be out for the USC game, as Sayin is out "indefinitely" with an undisclosed injury he suffered in the fourth quarter of the Indiana game and Jackson underwent foot surgery, according to a report from ESPN on Oct. 21. Timmons made his first appearance in two games against Indiana on Oct. 17 , recording seven tackles, two pass breakups and a forced fumble. But Timmons was pulled from the lineup once again and missed Ohio State's final defensive drives due to an apparent injury. "He plans on traveling," Ohio State coach Ryan Day said Oct. 28. "We'll kind of see how the next couple of days go." After Inniss had missed the Maryland matchup on Oct. 10 with an undisclosed injury, he played the full game against Indiana , logging one catch for 6 yards. The senior is tied for third for the Buckeyes with 11 receptions this season for 158 yards and one touchdown. Ohio State offensive lineman Austin Siereveld was notably left off the availability report after missing the previous two games due to illness. Day stated that Siereveld has returned to full practice this week, and he expects the senior to be an option, though is uncertain he'll be able to play the full game. The Buckeyes kick off at USC at 7:30 p.m. ET. If you purchase through our links, the USA Today Network may earn a commission. Prices were accurate at the time of publication but may change.

picks.headline: Know Thy Foe: Baylor Expert Shares What UCF Fans Need To Know For Space Game
picks.blurb: Know Thy Foe: Baylor Expert Shares What UCF Fans Need To Know For Space Game Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL RECRUITING COLLEGE FOOTBALL NEWS Olympic Sports More from UCF Knights On SI FOOTBALL While the UCF Knights may be coming off of one of the most significant wins in its program's history against No. 2 BYU on Saturday, they do not have long before they have to follow it up. The Baylor Bears may be entering their first game of the post-Dave Aranda era after firing him on Sunday, but they still have the same record as the Knights, and their interim coach, Joe Klanderman, has been in charge of a defense that has been one of the top five in the nation in sacks and tackles for loss. Jacob Haddaadin is both a Baylor graduate and a contributor for Baylor Bears on SI, and he took some time this week to answer some of our questions about the Bears (4-3, 2-2 Big 12): 1. How did the Bears reach a position in which they ended up firing their head coach midseason? Haddadin: Dave Aranda’s firing wasn't strictly due to this season's results. Ever since Dave Aranda won the Big 12 championship in 2021, the program has slowly trended downward. The Bears had real momentum after beating ASU in Tempe, but that momentum stalled after a double-digit home loss to TCU and a loss to a bad Kansas team in Lawrence. Dave Aranda had a losing record in the Big 12, a 1-6 record against rival TCU, and his teams were consistently unprepared in big games. We are forever grateful for the 12-2 season in 2021, but enough was enough, and Baylor fans were fed up with the constant expectation and disappointment cycle that was Dave Aranda. The loss to Kansas solidified that the Dave Aranda-led team was once again not going to be anything special. Cementing his exit from the program. 2. What’s the rundown on interim coach Joe Klanderman? What made him the choice to lead the program for the remainder of the season? Haddadin: Before Manhattan, Klanderman cut his teeth at North Dakota State, where he spent five years as defensive backs coach from 2014 to 2018, contributing to four FCS national championships. He then spent seven years at Kansas State, six of them running the defense, and K-State maintained a top-30 national ranking in defensive efficiency for five straight seasons through 2025. Part of what made him the choice is continuity. He was brought to Waco as one of the big offseason moves meant to turn things around; he’s already in the building, and the defense he built has been the most reliable part of this team. He has also come in with a clear plan, laying out three priorities for his time as interim head coach: energizing the program, strengthening the roster for 2027, and establishing complementary football to help Baylor win more games. He has been honest about where the problems are, too, pointing to the offensive line and the running game as the areas that need the most work. Whether or not this turns into a permanent job, the next five games give him a real chance to make his case, starting with a Friday night road game at UCF. 3. Quarterback DJ Lagway seems to have really connected with wide receiver Gavin Freeman, the latter of which is second in the nation in receptions per game and 14th in the nation in receiving yards. What makes Freeman such an oft-target wideout? Also, is there anyone else in the Bears’ receiving corps that could step up as a main target if Freeman is well-covered? Haddadin: Gavin Freeman’s production makes sense once you look at what he brings. At 5-9 and 189 pounds, he isn’t going to win many jump balls, but he has been reliable all season. He arrived as a redshirt senior after playing 2022-23 at Oklahoma and 2024-25 at Oklahoma State, and he was already a go-to receiver before coming to Waco, leading the Cowboys with 53 receptions for 481 yards and four scores in 2025. His fit with Lagway was clear from the first game, when he caught 12 passes for 154 yards and a touchdown in his Baylor debut against Auburn. It also helps that during the offseason, observers expected the passing game to work the middle of the field more, since Lagway is more comfortable there than Sawyer Robertson was. That is exactly where a quick, shifty slot receiver like Freeman does his best work. He has also produced when the offense hasn’t: in the 17-6 loss to TCU, he still caught seven passes for 76 yards. He adds value in other ways too. Last year at Oklahoma State, he contributed in both the passing and running game and as a returner. If defenses focus on Freeman, the most likely next option is Louis Brown IV. Before the season, he was described as the leader of the receiver room as one of its few upperclassmen with real experience in the offense, and he and Lagway connected well in the spring. Jadon Porter is another option to watch, and Baylor’s tight ends have been factors in the red zone. 4. Baylor is one of the most penalized teams in the Big 12. Is there one side of the ball that draws more flags? If so, why? Also, is there a particular penalty that gets called a lot? Haddadin: Most of the flags come from the offense, and specifically the offensive line. Through the early home stretch, one count found that the offense was outpacing the defense by nearly 3 to 1 in total penalties. The penalty that keeps showing up is the false start. Baylor had 5 against Prairie View A&M, 3 against Louisiana Tech, and 3 against Colorado, for at least 11 false starts in three home games. The Prairie View game was the low point: all four of Baylor’s false-start penalties were attributed to offensive lineman Asher Hale, and Aranda admitted afterward that one player had a bunch of penalties. Holding calls have added to the problem, but false starts are harder to excuse. ​A big reason is inexperience. The line was overhauled in the offseason and has been banged up in 2026, and while Baylor has capable players at each spot, most are new and started their first games together this year. Injuries haven’t helped either, including the injury to Koltin Sieracki, who was projected to be the best of the bunch but has not produced on the level the staff or fans expected. 5. The Bears have had a knack for getting behind the line of scrimmage this season, ranking in the top five in the nation in both sacks and tackles for loss. Who do they have to thank for that and what helps them get past offensive lines so often this season? Haddadin: The turnaround is remarkable given where this defense was a year ago. Baylor finished last season tied for last in the Big 12 and at the bottom of the FBS in sacks. Much of the credit goes to Klanderman and an offseason rebuild that put NIL money into the roster from the inside out. Defensive end Garrick Ponder leads the team with 3.5 sacks, Ryan Davis has added 2.5 off the edge, and Jordan Mack has chipped in 2.0. Up the middle, Hosea Wheeler and Traevon Mitchell occupy blockers and collapse the pocket, which opens lanes for everyone else. The most telling detail may be that two of the top three sack producers are safeties: Bo Onu and Daniel Cobbs have 3.0 sacks apiece. That says a lot about how Klanderman calls a game. He isn’t relying on one star pass rusher; six different players have at least two sacks, and he is willing to bring pressure from anywhere on the field, including the secondary. 6. What’s an aspect of this Bears team’s game that is not talked about enough? ​Haddadin: The most underrated part of this team might be the guy who comes on when the offense stalls. Senior punter Palmer Williams has quietly been one of the best weapons on the roster. He came into the year with plenty of credentials, as a 2025 All-American and Ray Guy Award finalist who earned first-team Walter Camp and second-team AP preseason All-American honors before this season. He picked up right where he left off. In the opener against Auburn, he punted four times for 208 yards, a 52-yard average, and earned Ray Guy Award Punter of the Week honors for flipping field position and helping Baylor get back into a game it nearly stole at the end. A month into the season, he was averaging over 50 yards a punt and consistently pinning punts near the goal line. He was a massive part of the win against Colorado in Week 4. As the offense struggled to move the ball, Williams flipped the field and pinned the Buffs inside their own 10-yard line on multiple occasions. If Friday’s game against UCF turns into a cagey field-position battle, Baylor won’t mind, since it has one of the best punters in the country. Pete Fiutak Thu, October 29, 2026 at 2:02 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Here's the punchline – both Baylor and UCF are 4-3 overall and 2-2 in Big 12 play. On one side, Baylor lost on the road to Kansas in a 25-24 fight, and that was it. Head coach Dave Aranda was fired, defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman is the interim head man, and the team needs this win with a tough November coming up. However, win in Orlando, beat Iowa State at home, and boom – the Bears are bowl-eligible. UCF lost on the road to Houston and Oklahoma State, and then it changed the national landscape – and got Scott Frost his first huge win in his second round with the Knights – with a 39-31 victory over BYU. With a very favorable finishing kick, UCF has to keep the momentum going. Baylor vs UCF: Quick Hits Baylor has the home date against Iowa State next, and then there's a problem – at BYU, Texas Tech, at Houston. UCF goes to Kansas after this, and then plays Arizona State, Iowa State, and goes to Colorado. None of those four are likely to go to a bowl game. It's the fourth meeting between the two. Baylor won 30-3 last year and won 36-35 in 2023, but UCF won a wild 52-42 Fiesta Bowl to end the 2013 season. How To Watch Baylor vs UCF Date: Friday, October 30, 2026 Game Time: 7:30 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando, FL – Week 9 Schedule, Game Previews – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predicting the First CFP Top 25 – CFN Week 9 Expert Picks Why Baylor Will Win The defense is taking the ball away in bunches. The run defense has been fantastic – Kansas ripped it up last week, but that was an anomaly – but the takeaways have been the biggest help, with 13 overall and at least two in four games. UCF doesn't have to get the running game going to win, but it's a huge help going 4-1 when running for more than 100 yards. Baylor has held four teams to under 100, but … Why UCF Will Win UCF isn't having a problem with turnovers. It has only given it up seven times, didn't turn it over against BYU, and it's +5 overall in turnover margin. So really, how did UCF beat BYU? The running game was effective enough – even if it wasn't dominant – and the passing game was fearless, and that's how the Knights have to play. They don't have to bomb away, but they should take the midrange plays against a Baylor pass defense that can get to the quarterback but is susceptible to quick hits. Baylor vs UCF Prediction, Betting Lines UCF needs to capitalize on the momentum, and it will. The Knights are 4-0 in the Bounce House, and 0-3 away from it. Baylor hung 55 at Arizona State and suffered two one-point losses away from Waco, but now it has to deal with the coaching drama and all the changes. The team will play hard and well for Klanderman, but the UCF offense will be just a bit more effective. The Knights have shown they can compete with the conference's top teams, making Friday's matchup an important test for Baylor's defense. When Baylor has the ball Baylor's passing attack will be one of its biggest advantages in this matchup. The Bears average 278.9 passing yards per game, and UCF surrenders 239.7 passing yards per game. Quarterback DJ Lagway will need to take advantage of that matchup and find opportunities downfield. Wide receiver Gavin Freeman has been one of Baylor's most consistent weapons, recording 58 receptions for 678 yards through seven games. His ability to create plays and stretch the field could be important against a UCF defense that has struggled more against the pass than the run. However, Baylor will need to establish a more consistent rushing attack. Dawson Pendergrass leads the Bears with 331 rushing yards, but the offense has averaged just 146.1 rushing yards per game. Finding balance between the run and pass will be important in keeping UCF's defense from focusing entirely on Lagway. When UCF has the ball The Knights rely on a balanced offensive attack led by quarterback Keyone Jenkins and running back Duke Watson. Jenkins has thrown for 1,099 yards and 11 touchdowns while Watson leads the team with 577 rushing yards and three touchdowns. Baylor's defensive front will need to pressure Jenkins and limit Watson's ability to establish the run. The Bears rank third nationally in sacks, giving them an opportunity to disrupt UCF's offensive rhythm. If Baylor can force third-and-long situations and create turnovers, it could make things difficult for a UCF offense that is coming off an emotional double-overtime victory. Baylor enters this matchup with plenty to prove after consecutive losses and a coaching change. While UCF has momentum following its win over BYU, the Bears have the defensive talent to make this a difficult matchup for the Knights. I expect Baylor to lean on its defense and take advantage of its passing game, with Freeman playing an important role. The Bears will need to clean up their mistakes and avoid giving UCF extra opportunities, but the Bears will find a way to get their first win under Klanderman. Score: Baylor 27, UCF 24. UCF enters the game riding high after stunning No. 2 BYU 39-31 in double overtime for the Knights' biggest win since joining the Big 12. Meanwhile, Baylor is beginning a new era after firing head coach Dave Aranda following Saturday's 25-24 loss to Kansas, with defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman taking over as interim head coach. Despite taking very different paths to get here, Baylor and UCF enter Friday night's game with identical 4-3 overall records and 2-2 marks in Big 12 play. For UCF, the question is whether Scott Frost's team can build off its breakthrough win or suffer a letdown. For Baylor, it's about what kind of response the Bears will have in their first game without Aranda. Here is everything you need to know about Baylor vs. UCF in Week 9, including our prediction and pick for Friday night's Big 12 matchup. Baylor vs. UCF Odds Spread: UCF -1.5 Over/Under: 48.5 Moneyline: UCF -120/Baylor +100 Odds as of Tuesday afternoon. Odds are subject to change. The Biggest Question: How do the emotions play a factor? The emotions on both sides of this game are tremendous. UCF is coming off of one of the biggest wins in program history over No. 2 BYU in double overtime at home. Now, they have to put that in the rearview mirror and take on Baylor. What' done is done. Have the Knights spent the last week in celebration mode? And then, on the other side, head coach Dave Aranda was fired on Sunday by Baylor. How does the team respond? How does defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman do in the interim role? There are so many unknowns going into this game, beyond the X's and O's, that ultimately will determine the outcome. Baylor vs. UCF Prediction and Pick Prediction: UCF 23, Baylor 20 It's a short week for both teams, but the good news for UCF is that they're playing their second-straight home game after a bye week. They haven't had to leave the friendly confines of Central Florida in nearly a month. Meantime, Baylor is getting set for its 3rd road game in its last four match ups, and their first without Aranda. In games like this, I try to find a nugget to sway me one way or the other, and here's what I've found: Baylor leads the Big 12 with 27 sacks in seven games. But one of the many things that UCF has done well with Keyone Jenkins is move the pocket, get rid of the ball quickly and avoid pressure in the backfield. BYU only had one sack last week against UCF, and the Knights have only allowed 10 in seven games, good for fourth fewest in the Big 12 Conference. Negating the pass rush by Baylor opens up a lot of opportunities for the UCF offense, and I believe that will be a game-changer on Friday night. Baylor has proven it can play with, and beat, some of the lesser Big 12 teams like Colorado and Arizona State. But even against just slightly better competition, TCU and Kansas, they came up short. UCF is one of the more underrated teams in the country, which I've been telling you since August. And despite their injuries, they're playing solid, team football, and that culminated with a with vs. BYU. But it was not a fluke. They led Houston in the second half on the road. They were beating Oklahoma State in Stillwater early in the game. This team can play with the best. Now, they get a chance to play one of the worst? I'll not overcomplicate this and take UCF to win and cover. Baylor's run defense ranks 4th in the Big 12, but they've already played the three worst running teams in the conference in Colorado, Arizona State and TCU. Now, they get Duke Watson, Jenkins and the rest of the run game going on Friday night to seal a win. UCF wins. UCF covers. away.headline: 5 Questionable Decisions That Defined Dave Aranda's Baylor Tenure
away.blurb: 5 Questionable Decisions That Defined Dave Aranda's Baylor Tenure Skip to main content SI.COM Here are five of the most questionable decisions of Aranda's Baylor tenure. Aranda had reason to overhaul Baylor's defensive staff following the 2022 season, but his choice of replacement proved questionable. Continuing to direct the defense while overseeing the entire program raised questions about whether Aranda had taken on too much. Although his defensive expertise was never in doubt, the arrangement potentially limited the attention he could devote to recruiting, roster construction and other head coaching duties. Dave Aranda's tenure at Baylor peaked in 2021, when the Bears won a program-record 12 games, captured the Big 12 championship and claimed a Sugar Bowl victory. Nearly five years later, he was fired following Saturday's 25-24 loss at Kansas, finishing his six-plus seasons in Waco with a 40-40 record. Baylor's decline can't be traced to a single mistake, but several of Aranda's decisions played a role in the program's inability to sustain its success. Some made sense at the time but ultimately backfired, while others were mistakes he later acknowledged. 1. Being Slow to Embrace the Transfer Portal Nov 22, 2025; Tucson, Arizona, USA; Detailed view of the jersey of Baylor Bears quarterback Sawyer Robertson (13) against the Arizona Wildcats at Casino Del Sol Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Aranda's emphasis on player development helped establish the culture behind Baylor's 2021 championship, but that same philosophy arguably kept the Bears from adapting quickly enough to college football's changing roster landscape. Aranda's emphasis on player development helped establish the culture behind Baylor's 2021 championship, but that same philosophy arguably kept the Bears from adapting quickly enough to college football's changing roster landscape. Baylor added only 10 scholarship transfers during Aranda's first three seasons before bringing in 12 during the 2023 cycle. While other programs increasingly used the portal to address immediate needs, the Bears remained more reliant on developing players already on their roster. Aranda later acknowledged struggling with bringing in transfers when doing so could mean passing over players he had recruited and developed. That reluctance became particularly costly following the 2021 season, when Baylor lost several important contributors, including Jalen Pitre, JT Woods, Terrel Bernard and Abram Smith. Replacing that experience and production was never going to be easy, but the transfer portal offered opportunities to address weaknesses before they became bigger problems. Instead, Baylor struggled to maintain the depth and physicality that had helped it win the conference championship. home.blurb: Running back LJ Martin is listed as out, while starting offensive guard Kyle Sfarcioc is questionable. Running back Sione Moa and safety Tommy Prassas are both expected to be available for the game. One is running back LJ Martin , the 2025 Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year. ESPN's Pete Thamel reported that he'd miss 4-6 weeks after the TCU game, meaning he has roughly 2-4 weeks remaining on that diagnosis. That injury was expected, as Martin is listed as "Out." Starting offensive guard Kyle Sfarcioc is the other Cougar listed on the injury report, as he has a "Questionable" designation going into the game. BYU's offensive line has been one of the nation's best, with Sfarcioc a big part of it. He missed the game against Notre Dame, and the Cougars handled his absence very well in giving quarterback Bear Bachmeier ample time to throw. But getting back the 6-foot-4, 305-pound redshirt senior would provide another boost to this group, one they might need against a pesky UCF defense. On the other side, the Knights have six players listed as out, one listed as doubtful, three listed as questionable and six listed as probable. The BYU Cougars will soon take the field to match up against the UCF Knights in a Week 8 Big 12 matchup, with the game kicking off at 1:00 p.m. MT on Saturday. And in that game, the Cougars will be very healthy. In the latest injury report, the Cougars have just two players listed. Also of note is that running back Sione Moa is not on the injury report, as he suffered an injury against Utah Tech in the season-opener and was sidelined — up until this week, it seems. He was cleared to play against Notre Dame, but wasn't a go for confidence reasons, offensive coordinator Aaron Roderick told reporters. Safety Tommy Prassas, the team's third-leading tackler (23), is also a full-go after dealing with his own injury. UCF’s upset of BYU reminded Scott Frost of glory days. Can they return?
home.blurb: News Sports Entertainment Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals UCF UCF’s upset of BYU reminded Scott Frost of glory days. Can they return? Chris Vinel Daytona Beach News-Journal Oct. 25, 2026, 10:51 a.m. ET UCF head coach Scott Frost recalled past program triumphs during a recent upset win over No. 2 BYU. “UCF has come so far so fast,” he said before stopping. “And listen, back up. We can’t pat ourselves on the back over this win. We have to play a really good Baylor team in six days. So I’ve got to get all this out now. Frost stated the program's next goal is to become a perennial threat in the Big 12 conference. ORLANDO — Scott Frost admits it’s funny where his mind wanders. “I get in these zones,” he said. Even in the closing moments of the UCF Knights’ stunning 39-31 upset of No. 2 BYU on Oct. 24, a victory they hope signals something for their future, the head coach turned backward. Two familiar names popped into his brain. “I was sitting there on the fourth down and I go ‘Tre Neal.’ I just wanted somebody to get an interception like Tre Neal did,” Frost said. “And they kick off to us, I’m thinking ‘Mike Hughes.’” Hughes, of course, took a kickoff for a 95-yard touchdown to win the 2017 War on I-4 against South Florida and complete UCF’s undefeated regular season. In the American Athletic Conference title game a week later, Neal grabbed a championship-sealing interception in double overtime against Memphis. That was the last time the Knights went past regulation prior to Saturday’s BYU showdown. Point being, it’s not just fans that get sucked into those memories of bygone triumphs. Frost draws the parallels, too. This fall, Frost has shown his current players videos of iconic UCF moments. How it put itself on the FBS map by downing Alabama in 2000. How it legitimized the AAC with a Fiesta Bowl win over Baylor , despite being a 17-point underdog, on New Year’s Day 2014. How it staked its national championship claim by beating Auburn in the Peach Bowl exactly four years later. That marked the final game of Frost’s first term in charge in Orlando. He returned ahead of the 2025 campaign to the same program but a completely different landscape of college football. “At the beginning of the year, we talked about playing with a chip on our shoulder and earning some respect,” Frost said. The Knights have been there before — in many of the instances mentioned above. But here’s the bad part about nostalgia: It’s a trap. The past guarantees nothing for today’s outcome and certainly not tomorrow’s. Frost caught himself during his postgame press conference. “But UCF has come so far so fast, and we’ve cleared so many hurdles to get into the Big 12 and get where we are.” Then, the reflection ended, and Frost aimed forward. “The biggest hurdle we’ve got to clear is now being competitive and a winning program and then hopefully a perennial threat in the Big 12,” he said. “... Hopefully, this will boost us a little.”
